item.title: Bayern Munich might be sweating over Michael Olise injury after crutches sighting
item.description: (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich could be facing another unwelcome setback on the injury front, with Michael Olise’s status now looking increasingly concerning after his early exit against 1. FC Köln. The winger was unable to make it through the opening 45 minutes, leaving the game at halftime after picking up an injury during the first half. Olise initially attempted to carry on after receiving attention, but Bayern Mu nich ultimately opted to take him off rather than risk aggravating the problem. Tim Binder came on in his place after the brea k. There is now an additional reason for concern. Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenb erg reports that — per Sky commentators — Olise left the stadium on crutches, an image that certainly does not inspire confidence while Bayern Munich awaits a clearer picture of the injury: 🚨Michael Olise left the stadium on crutches, according to the Sky commentators. https://t.co/qWC3ZPvpEt — Florian Plettenberg (@Plettigoal) November 20, 2026 No definitive diagnosis or recovery timeline has been established yet. Bayern Munich will need medical examinations to determine whether this is a short-term scare or something considerably more serious. Hopefully, this report will be proven untrue because, if not, this could be a tough spell for the Bavarians. Join the conversation! item.title: Houston visits West Virginia with consecutive 10-win seasons within reach: 5 things to watch
item.description: Quarterback Conner Weigman is 17-6 Houston's starter going into Saturday's game at West Virginia. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - With an extra day to prepare this week, coach Willie Fritz went through every aspect of the University of Houston 's 42-32 loss at Colorado. "We looked at every second of the tape from the Colorado game and made corrections," said Fritz, whose No. 20 Cougars make their first visit Saturday to face West Virginia at Milan Puskar Stadium . "Sometimes you have to move on to the next game. "We did that the week before (Cincinnati) because it was a short week and we wanted to move on, so we watched a little bit of the tape. (But this week) we watched every single snap to take ownership of calls and assignments, and just make sure we don't repeat the same mistakes." With two games left in the regular season and a bowl, the Cougars (7-3, 4-3 Big 12) are still chasing consecutive 10-win seasons for the first time in the program's 80-year history. To get there, though, the Cougars will have to reverse a trend this season. UH is 5-0 at TDECU Stadium this season but only 2-3 on the road. Here are five things to watch as the Cougars play the Mountaineers: Play four quarters The Cougars have led by double-digits in all three losses this season before things unraveled. UH had a 20-7 lead before Colorado scored 14 points in the final two minutes before halftime. It was the same story against Texas Tech and Utah, which resulted in close losses to the Big 12's top two teams in the standings. In all three games, the offense and defense have struggled to complement each other for the entire 60 minutes. Against Colorado, the Cougars hummed along for most of the first half before the defense repeatedly got torched by explosive plays over the final three quarters. UH can't afford any lengthy offensive lulls (six drives produced 69 yards vs. Colorado) with West Virginia's ability to put up points in a hurry. "We're looking forward to rebounding," Fritz said. item.content:encoded: Quarterback Conner Weigman is 17-6 Houston's starter going into Saturday's game at West Virginia. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - With an extra day to prepare this week, coach Willie Fritz went through every aspect of the University of Houston 's 42-32 loss at Colorado. "We looked at every second of the tape from the Colorado game and made corrections," said Fritz, whose No. 20 Cougars make their first visit Saturday to face West Virginia at Milan Puskar Stadium . "Sometimes you have to move on to the next game. "We did that the week before (Cincinnati) because it was a short week and we wanted to move on, so we watched a little bit of the tape. (But this week) we watched every single snap to take ownership of calls and assignments, and just make sure we don't repeat the same mistakes." With two games left in the regular season and a bowl, the Cougars (7-3, 4-3 Big 12) are still chasing consecutive 10-win seasons for the first time in the program's 80-year history. To get there, though, the Cougars will have to reverse a trend this season. UH is 5-0 at TDECU Stadium this season but only 2-3 on the road. Here are five things to watch as the Cougars play the Mountaineers: Play four quarters The Cougars have led by double-digits in all three losses this season before things unraveled. UH had a 20-7 lead before Colorado scored 14 points in the final two minutes before halftime. It was the same story against Texas Tech and Utah, which resulted in close losses to the Big 12's top two teams in the standings. In all three games, the offense and defense have struggled to complement each other for the entire 60 minutes. Against Colorado, the Cougars hummed along for most of the first half before the defense repeatedly got torched by explosive plays over the final three quarters. UH can't afford any lengthy offensive lulls (six drives produced 69 yards vs. Colorado) with West Virginia's ability to put up points in a hurry. "We're looking forward to rebounding," Fritz said. Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . Are the Mountaineers motivated? To become bowl eligible, West Virginia (5-5, 2-5 Big 12) must beat either UH or Utah. The Cougars might offer the Mountaineers' best chance. West Virginia closes the regular season in Salt Lake City against No. 2 Utah, which could already have clinched a spot in the Big 12 championship game and will be seeking to lock up a top-four seed in the College Football Playoff. Even with an early kickoff, Fritz said Morgantown can be noisy and the Cougars spent the week piping in John Denver's "Take Me Home, Country Roads," West Virginia's official state song. "It's going to be loud," Fritz said. Limit explosive plays That goes without saying after the Cougars surrendered four touchdowns of at least 32 yards. Fritz said there's "a lot of room for improvement" as the Cougars struggled with leverage and angles and had coverage breakdowns that allowed Colorado to rush for a season-high 249 yards. UH's defense has been inconsistent and has shown cracks late in the season, not exactly comforting against a West Virginia offense that averages 34.9 points per game, which ranks 20th nationally (one spot behind the Cougars). Two weeks ago, the Mountaineers got into a shootout with Texas Tech before falling short 53-48. If there's a bright spot for the Cougars, West Virginia's defense has experienced its share of struggles this season. The Mountaineers rank last in the Big 12 in rushing defense, passing defense, total defense and scoring defense. Prepare for the run The Cougars can expect a heavy dose of the running game with the Mountaineers on the verge of a pair of 1,000-yard rushers. A year after leading the nation with 1,659 yards at Jacksonville State, Cam Cook has rushed for 1,084 yards and eight touchdowns. He has six 100-yard games, including a stretch that produced 193 (Oklahoma State), 142 (Iowa State) and 141 yards (Arizona). Michael Hawkins Jr. has thrown for 2,128 yards and 13 touchdowns but is equally dangerous as a runner, with 957 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns. Hawkins accounted for 391 yards and four touchdowns against Texas Tech. West Virginia is sixth nationally, averaging 240.7 rushing yards per game. One big question: Which Mountaineers offense will show up? In last week's 37-14 home loss to basement-dweller Kansas, West Virginia was held to a a season-low points and just 35 yards on the ground. Consistent Conner As his college career nears the end, UH quarterback Conner Weigman is looking to finish strong. Weigman has thrown for 2,552 yards and 25 touchdowns this season. In two seasons at UH, Weigman has accounted for 68 total touchdowns, which leads all Power Four quarterbacks during that span. Weigman is 17-6 as UH's starter, the fifth-most wins nationally. Weigman has been especially careful with the ball with only three interceptions, including two on pass deflections. He's also lost a fumble on a strip-sack in each of the Cougars' losses. "He's had a great season, he really has," Fritz said. "He's kind of going up the draft boards, which is very, very deserving. We want to make sure he goes out a winner here." item.title: 2026 NCAA Women’s Soccer Tournament: Purdue 4, Southern Illinois 0
item.description: ST LOUIS, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 5: Irene Campo #14 of the Purdue Boilermakers celebrates with teammates after scoring the game winning goal against the Penn State Nittany Lions in extra time of the quarterfinals round of the 2026 Big Ten Soccer Championship at Energizer Park on November 5, 2026 in St Louis, Missouri. (Photo by Jeff Curry/Big Ten/University Images via Getty Images) Purdue’s return to the women’s NCAA soccer Tournament will last a bit longer. This afternoon the Boilers kicked off the entire tournament with the opening match of the whole show. They also left little doubt as they moved on with a dominant 4-0 win over Southern Illinois. This was a match where Purdue controlled possession and was never seriously threatened throughout. In fact, Southern Illinois didn’t even have a shot in the first half compared to 14 by Purdue. The Boilers got goals from McKenzie Carle in the 18th minute and Tanna Schornstein in the 26th minute to hold a comfortable 2-0 lead at halftime. The second half saw Irene Campo get a brace with goals at the 52nd and 67th minute, giving her a hand in all four Purdue goals after she assisted on both in the first half This continued Purdue’s dominant run over the past few weeks that has seen it become the best offensive team in the nation. Coming into today’s game Jaiden Anderson was the country’s leading goalscorer with 20 and as a team Purdue’s 74 goals was the best in Division I. Purdue now awaits the winner of tonight’s other first round match between 5 seed Texas and Houston. 1 seed Ohio State wins their opening match I believe the second round match would be played in Columbus next weekend, as the Buckeyes would host both second round matches and the Sweet 16 match with the way the bracket lines up. Purdue fell to the Buckeyes 2-1 earlier this season for one of just two losses it has suffered all year.

item.title: 44 Years Later, Steven Spielberg's Scariest Movie of All Time Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.description: Poltergeist , which became available to stream for free on Pluto TV on Nov. 1 , follows an ordinary suburban family that begins to experience strange things in their home. Furniture and toys move on their own, a glass of milk shatters out of nowhere, and the youngest child in the family, 5-year-old Carol Anne (Heather O'Rourke), begins to communicate with beings through the television. At first, these events are dismissed, but during a thunderstorm one night, a tree outside the windows of the kids’ room crashes in and snatches the boy. Then, a portal opens in their closet, sucking Carol Anne into another dimension. With help from some paranormal investigators, the family tries everything to bring her back.

item.title: Fan Attending Cowboys-49ers Game Dies Days After Falling During In-Stadium ‘Altercation’
item.description: AT&T Stadium - Home to the Dallas Cowboys Credit: Nicole Cordeiro NEED TO KNOW A football fan died days after being involved in a fight at the Dallas Cowboys’ AT&T Stadium Mario Narro, 36, died on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at an Arlington, Texas hospital Narro fell during a fight before kickoff, but stayed to watch most of the game before he sought medical attention A 36-year-old man has died days after he was involved in a fight with another fan at a Dallas Cowboys game. Mario Narro died on Wednesday, Nov. 18 in the ICU at Medical City Arlington Hospital, according to the Tarrant County Medical Examiner and NBC 5 . His cause of death is currently pending, according to the ME’s office. Narro’s family members told the Arlington Police Department that he fell during an altercation at AT&T Stadium before kickoff, but that Narro stayed to watch most of the game between the Cowboys and the San Francisco 49ers before he began to complain of discomfort, according to NBC 5. AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Tx. Credit: typhoonski / Getty Images A friend alerted stadium paramedics who then worked to transport him to the local hospital, KERA News reported . Narro’s family submitted a police report on Nov. 17, the day before he died on Wednesday morning. The APD has opened an investigation into Narro’s death, and is reviewing surveillance from the stadium, per NBC 5. The NFC rivalry game, which featured a hearty contingent of Niners fans, was the site of numerous fights on Sunday. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! On social media , one such fracas involving two women went viral. The two fans wrestled on the ground of the stadium’s concourse as onlookers watched, while another fight between two men occurred in the background. The brawls occurred minutes after the game concluded, in which the 49ers beat up the home team, 46-40. The Cowboys next host the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Read the original article on People

item.title: Vikings’ Kyler Murray, Jordan Addison are out, but TJ Hockenson receives good injury update
item.description: Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, left, talks to Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) after 19-15 win at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Vikings’ Kyler Murray, Jordan Addison are out, but TJ Hockenson receives good injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Kevin O’Connell’s Minnesota Vikings are 7-2, tied for the NFC North lead, but have a huge task ahead of them with a road trip to Mexico City to play the 49ers on the docket. The Kyle Shanahan vs. Brian Flores coaching matchup looks like a high-level chess match , but the Vikings’ offense is also key with injuries rearing their ugly head. ESPN’s Adam Schefter shared the latest news on the Vikings’ offensive injuries, and it was a mixed bag for OC Wes Phillips’ group. “TJ Hockensen is off the Vikings injury report and good to go Sunday night,” he wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Receiver Jordan Addison and quarterback Kyler Murray are listed as out, while defensive backs Isaiah Rodgers and Jay Ward are listed as questionable. The Vikings’ Kirk Cousins-led offense exploded for 39 points in a win over the Packers in Week 11, but hasn’t put up a ton of points this season with Minnesota relying on Flores’ defense to lead the way. Cousins’ arrival has helped O’Connell’s team turn over a new leaf, adding to a passing game that needed better efficiency, leadership, accuracy, and big play potential. Murray’s stint with the Vikings has been a disappointing one health-wise and stats-wise, but he has done his part to make O’Connell’s team a contender amid a rapidly shifting roster each week. The Vikings could get extra help against the 49ers from Jauan Jennings, who is excited to play his former team in Mexico City. The Vikings’ passing game has plenty of weapons, but so does the 49ers’. A shootout could unfold, or Flores’ defense could put the clamps on San Francisco in one of Week 12’s most exciting matchups by far. item.title: Texans’ C.J. Stroud draws intriguing Joe Burrow comparison
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Texans’ C.J. Stroud draws intriguing Joe Burrow comparison appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans are now 4-6 on the season after stomping the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on “Thursday Night Football” in Week 11 thanks to another solid outing from quarterback C.J. Stroud. While the 25-year-old signal-caller has yet to sign a contract extension with the club, he is at least doing his part to keep the team competitive. After another good game, Colin Cowherd couldn’t help but compare Stroud to Joe Burrow . Cowherd’s comparison had more to do with the contract situation for Burrow right before he signed his five-year, $275 million extension. The popular sports analyst claims that the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t do enough to build around Burrow before giving him his extension, and feels Stroud is in a similar situation with the Texans. “C.J. Stroud has had a great season, and now the Texans are trapped,” Cowherd said… “I feel like he’s going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn’t get it done enough before he signed the big deal.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "C.J. Stroud has had a great season and now the Texans are trapped… I feel like he's going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn't get it done enough before he signed the big deal." @colincowherd on C.J. Stroud & the Texans pic.twitter.com/Of7YQ5dM0Y — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) November 20, 2026 The Texans initially went into the 2026-27 campaign believed to have the best defense in football, while questions surrounded Stroud about whether or not he is a franchise quarterback. Fast forward to Week 11, and the storyline is seemingly the opposite. Even though Houston has struggled throughout the campaign, the four-year veteran is putting up solid numbers, throwing for 2,656 yards, 22 touchdowns, and four interceptions with a 64.0% completion percentage through 10 games. Stroud is well on pace to throw for the most touchdowns in a single season in his career, as he’s just one shy of tying his career record of 23 set in his rookie year. If the defense can somehow get to the level of play it was last season, then the Texans could be a huge problem in the back end of the 2026-27 campaign. C.J. Stroud and his teammates will enjoy a mini-bye after playing on TNF. Houston will next play in Week 12 at home against the Baltimore Ravens. Stroud has had a great season, and now the Texans are trapped,” Cowherd said… “I feel like he’s going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn’t get it done enough before he signed the big deal.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "C.J. Stroud has had a great season and now the Texans are trapped… I feel like he's going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn't get it done enough before he signed the big deal." @colincowherd on C.J. Stroud & the Texans pic.twitter.com/Of7YQ5dM0Y — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) November 20, 2026 The Texans initially went into the 2026-27 campaign believed to have the best defense in football, while questions surrounded Stroud about whether or not he is a franchise quarterback. Fast forward to Week 11, and the storyline is seemingly the opposite. Even though Houston has struggled throughout the campaign, the four-year veteran is putting up solid numbers, throwing for 2,656 yards, 22 touchdowns, and four interceptions with a 64.0% completion percentage through 10 games. Stroud is well on pace to throw for the most touchdowns in a single season in his career, as he’s just one shy of tying his career record of 23 set in his rookie year. item.title: Knicks superfan Ben Stiller recalls losing his mind over Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. Pistons in 2025 playoffs
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images. Knicks superfan Ben Stiller recalls losing his mind over Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. Pistons in 2025 playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of the most memorable moments of New York Knicks superfan Ben Stiller was Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. the Detroit Pistons during the 2025 playoffs. A fan responded to a post asking what the “greatest” non- OG Anunoby tip-in play in Knicks history was. One fan responded with a clip of Brunson’s game-winner in Game 6 of the Knicks-Pistons series last year, saying, “This s**t literally made Me lose my mind,” to which Stiller replied, “Me too.” Me too. https://t.co/NiNxCoU521 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Ben Stiller (@BenStiller) November 20, 2026 The play was huge. The game was tied at 113 before Brunson hit his three-pointer with about four seconds left in the game. Detroit was unable to score on their next possession. Brunson ended the game with 40 points. He also had four rebounds and seven assists. He was the Knicks’ leading scorer that night. This won the series for the Knicks, who advance to the Eastern Conference Semifinals. They made it all the way to the Eastern Conference Finals that year before losing to the Indiana Pacers. The following year, the Knicks made it to the NBA Finals. They beat the San Antonio Spurs in five games to win their first championship in 53 years. Stiller is one of the most famous celebrity fans of the Knicks. He has been filming footage for an upcoming documentary about the team dating back to their playoff run earlier in 2026. The Knicks have gotten back on track after a disastrous 0-3 start. They have won three games in a row, including two straight against the Toronto Raptors, and just beat the Minnesota Timberwolves. They survived a four-game road trip and will play their next five games at home, including a Black Friday matchup with the Miami Heat. The Knicks will also play the Portland Trail Blazers, the Pacers, the Cleveland Cavaliers, and the Atlanta Hawks in this home stretch. Other series you can look forward to soon include Alien: Earth season 2 and Neuromancer . This month, Blade Runner 2099 is premiering on Prime Video.

item.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
item.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

item.title: Juventus reignites interest in Manchester United star
item.description: Juventus reignites interest in Manchester United star Juventus are once again interested in signing Joshua Zirkzee as they look to strengthen their attacking options during the January transfer window. The Dutch striker was among their targets last summer when he was open to leaving Manchester United in search of regular playing time. The Bianconeri explored the possibility of signing him on loan, but they faced competition from several other clubs, including teams in the Premier League. At the time, Benjamin Sesko was identified as United’s preferred striker, which appeared to leave Zirkzee’s future uncertain. However, none of the potential moves materialised, giving Juventus another opportunity to pursue the forward. The Old Lady are keen to take advantage of the situation and could return with a fresh approach when the transfer window opens. Juventus revive their interest in Zirkzee Juventus regard Zirkzee as one of the attractive options available in the market and would like to bring him to Turin. Nevertheless, his situation at Manchester United could depend on the plans of Mauricio Pochettino, who has recently been appointed as the club’s manager. The Argentine will first need to assess the players available to him before making decisions about their respective futures. Zirkzee’s prospects could therefore become clearer once the new manager has evaluated his squad and decided which players fit into his plans. A decision from Pochettino could have an important influence on Juventus’ pursuit, particularly if the striker is allowed to leave in January. Bianconeri want attacking reinforcements According to Football Italia , Juventus remain interested in signing Zirkzee because they have not been satisfied with the performances of their current strikers. The report adds that Juventus intend to recruit a new forward in January, with the United attacker among the players they would particularly like to add to their squad. For Juventus, bringing in Zirkzee could provide another option in attack as they look to improve their attacking output . However, much will depend on Manchester United’s willingness to sanction his departure and whether Pochettino sees a future for the Dutchman at Old Trafford. A January move remains a possibility as Juventus continue to assess their options ahead of the transfer window.

item.title: Naomi Osaka issues statement as her 2026 season ends after ‘extreme eye-opener’ this year
item.description: Naomi Osaka’s 2026 season came to an end last month in front of a home crowd in Tokyo. The Japanese star played just 13 tournaments this year, including all four Grand Slams and six WTA 1000 events. But following the resurgent second half of her 2025 season, during which she made the semifinals of the US Open and the final of the Canadian Open, Osaka has not quite kicked on in 2026. While she reached the final in Bad Homburg and the quarterfinals of Wimbledon for the first time, the 29-year-old has not been able to rediscover the level that saw her win four Grand Slam titles from 2018 to 2021. Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Naomi Osaka releases statement on social media about her season In a post on Instagram , Osaka said: “Someone asked me for a season recap haha. This year has been an extreme eye-opener for me. I used to think I needed permission and approval to be myself, that I was weird for the things I wanted to express and create. “Turns out I was wrong, and the more I trusted my ideas and embraced my uniqueness, the happier and more fulfilled I became. This year is dedicated for anyone who feels a little different and is having a hard time navigating it- you’ll find yourself I promise.” Perhaps Osaka’s most impressive run in 2026 came at the Wimbledon championships, a tournament that, historically, she had struggled at. Prior to this season, Osaka had never made it past the third round of the grass court major across five appearances. But this year, Osaka made huge improvements on grass, reaching the final of the Bad Homburg Open without dropping a set. She was forced to retire during the championship match at the WTA 500 event against Karolina Muchova. Osaka’s impressive grass-court form continued into Wimbledon, where she reached the quarterfinals by beating then-world number one Aryna Sabalenka. Osaka was ultimately knocked out of the tournament by Muchova. After her run at Wimbledon, Osaka made the semifinals in Washington and the quarterfinals of the Canadian Open, but was beaten in the fourth round of the US Open by eventual champion Elena Rybakina. Osaka finished the year with an indifferent Asian swing and ended 2026 ranked 17th in the world, one spot lower than where she started the season.

item.title: UFC Qatar’s Alessandro Costa seeks 4th win in 2026, pitches backup role for Joshua Van vs. Manel Kape
item.description: Alessandro Costa and Amir Albazi first fought in 2022 | Chris Unger, Zuffa LLC Alessandro Costa enters the octagon Saturday to rematch Amir Albazi at UFC Qatar, looking to avenge his first octagon loss after already finishing three opponents in 2026, and plans to take the rest of the year off to rest his body after an intense run. Or maybe not. Between April and July, a span of 99 days, Costa stopped Stewart Nicoll, Matt Schnell and Cody Durden, each in under 10 minutes, and returns Saturday to close out the year on an ever higher note in Doha. The Albazi rematch is the fight he called for going into his clash with Durden, and the one he got after all. Winning in Qatar would make 2026 the best year of his MMA career, and Costa is willing to make an exception for his break if the UFC needs a backup fighter for the upcoming title bout between Joshua Van and Manel Kape, the headlining attraction for UFC 336 on Jan. 30 in Toronto. “My dream comes first, right?” Costa told MMA Fighting. “If I feel like an opportunity is going to come up, I’ll definitely be there, man. I’ll get some rest, but I’ll let them know, ‘If anything happens, I’m here. Just give me a call.’” “It seems like everything is going well [with Kape],” he continued. “He’s doing things differently now. He’s also a guy who struggles a little with his weight, but anything can happen. We have to be ready when the call comes.” There are no clear-cut contenders in the division at the moment, with the winner of UFC Qatar’s Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev definitely gaining traction on the run. Costa, although unranked at the moment, believes “anything can happen” under today’s UFC modus operandi. “The title fight could fall through and other fighters might not be ready,” Costa said. “I’m here. This is a time when a lot of surprises can happen. I think anyone could get the opportunity to fight for the title. That’s why I decided this year to be better prepared and ready for any opportunity, and it’s been paying off. I think anyone from No. 15 all the way up to the champion has a chance to fight for the title. You just have to be ready.” Costa has called for Albazi for the past three years and is confident he’s a much better fighter than the one who shared the octagon with Albazi that night in 2022. “I had some health issues when we fought and couldn’t compete at 100 percent,” Costa said. “It was my debut. Of course, that’s no excuse. He’s very good, but I know my potential, and I know I could have put on a very different performance. He was in his prime, undefeated, and I remember accepting the fight on nine days’ notice. But things are completely different now. I have more UFC experience. The story is a little different now, right? I’m coming off three wins, he’s coming off two losses, but I’m definitely not underestimating him. I trust my work. I’ve worked on improving every area where I made mistakes in our first fight, and you can be sure things will be completely different this time.” “

I’ll end the year by making history. I’m very motivated and very happy about it.”

item.title: Arizona cross country prepared for uphill race at NCAA Championships
item.description: On Saturday the Arizona men’s cross country team will step up to the starting line with 31 other teams at the NCAA Championships. Competing at the championship meet is unfamiliar terrain for Arizona, a program that last made NCAA Championships in 2006. The course Arizona will be running on in Terre Haute, Indiana, however, is one the Arizona men — and women’s individual competitor Mercy Chepkemoi — are actually quite familiar with. That’s because Arizona competed last month at the Under Armor Pre-National Invitational, held at the LaVern Gibson Championship Cross Country Course in Terre Haute. Terre Haute, affectionally known in college cross country as Terradise, features one of the few courses specifically designed for the sport. According to Indiana State University, the course’s popularity is due to a mix of uphill and downhill sections that complement a simple straightaway start. Running up and down hills tests distance runners in ways than a relatively flat course doesn’t. It forces athletes to endure greater resistance (uphill) and navigate unique stresses (downhill). Arizona cross country coach Jay Koloseus said the team has worked all season on inclines in preparation for the type of course they’ll see Saturday. “Obviously we’re blessed to be close to the mountains here,” Koloseus said. “But it was also learning last year we were quite surprised we got to a course and it was very hilly.” When Arizona competed at the Pre-National Invitational in October, the team was less fearful for the LaVern Gibson course having done workout paces going up hills, Koloseus said. “I’m not going to say enjoyable, but it was really nice to see the athletes this year now that we’ve seen all the courses we’re going to see with big hills do their warmup run on it or practice the day before,” he said. “They all come back and say, ‘Wow, we’ve all done hills much worse than this,’ where last year we finished a few course jogs and you could see they were just kind of freaked out.“ The Arizona men took sixth at the Pre-National Invitational in a field that was competitive but not representative of what the Wildcats will face on Saturday. Arizona enters the meet ranked No. 28 in the country and is coming off a fifth-place finish at NCAA Regionals. The Wildcats are led by Evans Tanui , who has been the team’s top finisher in every meet this fall. Tanui, who competed as an individual at last year’s NCAA Championship, has a good opportunity of becoming Arizona’s first men’s All-American since Stephen Sambu in 2012. To do so Tanui needs to finish in the top 40. Josphat Meli and Vincent Gwachi have been Arizona’s next top two runners this season, with Lawi Ngetich and Hanibal Haile also competing for points. In a cross country team event, the top five finishers count to a team’s score. Competing at the championship meet is unfamiliar terrain for Arizona, a program that last made NCAA Championships in 2006. The course Arizona will be running on in Terre Haute, Indiana, however, is one the Arizona men — and women’s individual competitor Mercy Chepkemoi — are actually quite familiar with. That’s because Arizona competed last month at the Under Armor Pre-National Invitational, held at the LaVern Gibson Championship Cross Country Course in Terre Haute. Terre Haute, affectionally known in college cross country as Terradise, features one of the few courses specifically designed for the sport. According to Indiana State University, the course’s popularity is due to a mix of uphill and downhill sections that complement a simple straightaway start. Running up and down hills tests distance runners in ways than a relatively flat course doesn’t. It forces athletes to endure greater resistance (uphill) and navigate unique stresses (downhill). Arizona cross country coach Jay Koloseus said the team has worked all season on inclines in preparation for the type of course they’ll see Saturday. “Obviously we’re blessed to be close to the mountains here,” Koloseus said. “But it was also learning last year we were quite surprised we got to a course and it was very hilly.” When Arizona competed at the Pre-National Invitational in October, the team was less fearful for the LaVern Gibson course having done workout paces going up hills, Koloseus said. “I’m not going to say enjoyable, but it was really nice to see the athletes this year now that we’ve seen all the courses we’re going to see with big hills do their warmup run on it or practice the day before,” he said. “They all come back and say, ‘Wow, we’ve all done hills much worse than this,’ where last year we finished a few course jogs and you could see they were just kind of freaked out.“ The Arizona men took sixth at the Pre-National Invitational in a field that was competitive but not representative of what the Wildcats will face on Saturday. Arizona enters the meet ranked No. 28 in the country and is coming off a fifth-place finish at NCAA Regionals. The Wildcats are led by Evans Tanui , who has been the team’s top finisher in every meet this fall. Tanui, who competed as an individual at last year’s NCAA Championship, has a good opportunity of becoming Arizona’s first men’s All-American since Stephen Sambu in 2012. To do so Tanui needs to finish in the top 40. Josphat Meli and Vincent Gwachi have been Arizona’s next top two runners this season, with Lawi Ngetich and Hanibal Haile also competing for points. In a cross country team event, the top five finishers count to a team’s score. Only seven runners get to compete per team, making the selection process a hard decision for any coach. “We have a group of 10 men who all realize, ‘Hey, I’m exceptional. I just happen to be on one of the best teams we’ve seen in a while, and and I can push the guy in front of me and pull up the guy behind me,’” Koloseus said. On the women’s side, Chepkemoi is poised to be Arizona’s first female All-American since Claire Green in 2017. The freshman has finished near the top of the pack in every race this season. How to follow The NCAA Championships take place Saturday morning, with the women’s 6K race set for 8:20 a.m. MST and the men’s 10K to follow at 9:10 a.m. MST. Live results can be found here . The meet will be aired on ESPNU.

item.title: Barcelona tracking Girona starlet Holmes Junior Zamorano
item.description: TALLINN, ESTONIA - JUNE 04: Holmes Junior of Spain arrives at the stadium prior to the UEFA European Under-17 Championship 2026 Semi-final match between Italy and Spain at Lillekula staadion on June 04, 2026 in Tallinn, Estonia. (Photo by Harry Murphy - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Barcelona are reportedly monitoring Girona and Spain Under-17 youngster Holmes Junior Zamorano and have been tracking the teenage talent “for some time.” Holmes Junior began his career at Real Madrid but joined Girona in 2025 and has made eight starts for the club this season in La Liga. A source has told ESPN that Barcelona “see him as having the potential to make the leap to elite football in the future” and appreciate his versatility. Holmes is a left-footed center-back but can also play at left-back and in midfield. Barca aren’t the only club keen on the defender, with clubs in the Premier League and Germany also expressing interest. The 17-year-old isn’t the only young defender on Barca’s radar right now. The club are also being linked with Ruud Nijstad , with the club potentially set to bring in a young defender in the summer. Holmes is currently with the Spain squad for the Under-17 World Cup where he will play alongside several Barcelona starlets including Ebrima Tunkara .

item.title: SBN Reacts: Mizzou Fans Want the Vegas Bowl
item.description: ATHENS, GA - NOVEMBER 14: Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz prior to the college football game between the Missouri Tigers and Georgia Bulldogs on November 14, 2026, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by John Adams/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Missouri Tigers are out of the CFP race after a 48-21 loss to Georgia last week, dropping to 6-4 overall aand 3-4 in SEC play. Mizzou will hope to finish the season strong in the final two weeks of the regular season as they host No. 16 Kentucky tomorrow night, and No. 22 Oklahoma next Saturday. Missouri will have the opportunity to improve their bowl positioning. We asked the fanbase which bowl game do Mizzou fans want the most — and the Vegas Bowl was the popular pick. The Vegas Bowl is set for Thursday, December 31st at 2:45 p.m. CST on ESPN at Allegiant Stadium — which pairs an SEC team vs a Big Ten team. Missing out on the College Football Playoff stings for sure, but a trip to Vegas for Mizzou fans wouldn’t be a bad consolation prize. Missouri has more work to do to finish off the season on a high note, and the Tigers are currently 4.5-point favorites over No. 16 Kentucky — per the Week 12 CFB lines over at our partners over on FanDuel Sportsbook .

item.title: Pick Six: New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Austin Ekeler #30 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs in a touchdown against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are, embarrassingly, a three-point underdog on Sunday against a team who didn’t earn their first win until less than a week ago. The Los Angeles Chargers will be looking to build on their 23-20 win over the Ravens, and the Jets are making the long trip out west to take them on. Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to inject some positivity into their season: Playing the slots Last week, we discussed the Jets’ varying options for their slot cornerback position and they eventually went with one of our suggestions, which was to primarily use Minkah Fitzpatrick there in nickel packages, bringing Malachi Moore off the bench to fill in at safety. The Jets potentially face a similar dilemma in the slot this week, albeit on offense. Both Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams have been unable to practice, so if neither can go on Sunday, the Jets will have to make a change. One option could be to go with the guys currently on the roster. You could reactivate Jelani Woods and Tim Patrick and either run more multiple tight end packages, or use players like Garrett Wilson there. Another option could be to bring up Sterling Shepard or Jamaal Pritchett from the practice squad. The job share at running back remains a work in progress The Jets are still trying to figure out how to get the best out of Braelon Allen and Breece Hall now that both are healthy at the same time. Allen’s performances while Hall was out proved that he can benefit from a bigger workload. However, Hall brings different things to the table in the passing game, so the Jets will want him on the field more often than not. Last week was interesting because they employed Hall more in the passing game in the first half with Allen getting more carries. At the half, Allen had six carries and Hall had just two. However, after halftime, Allen carried the ball just twice and Hall had nine carries. It’s possible the Jets’ thinking was that Hall might produce better after halftime if he was fresh and the defense was tired. In the end, the pair had similar rushing numbers, but Hall produced more as a receiver. You can probably expect the Jets to keep working on this with one option being flipping last week’s gameplan on its head and using Hall early, then keeping Allen fresh to be the hammer in the second half. The Chargers’ run defense did a great job against the Ravens, holding them to 16 yards on 15 carries, so it might not be easy to get a running game established. Will Daiyan Henley play? item.content:encoded: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Austin Ekeler #30 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs in a touchdown against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are, embarrassingly, a three-point underdog on Sunday against a team who didn’t earn their first win until less than a week ago. The Los Angeles Chargers will be looking to build on their 23-20 win over the Ravens, and the Jets are making the long trip out west to take them on. Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to inject some positivity into their season: Playing the slots Last week, we discussed the Jets’ varying options for their slot cornerback position and they eventually went with one of our suggestions, which was to primarily use Minkah Fitzpatrick there in nickel packages, bringing Malachi Moore off the bench to fill in at safety. The Jets potentially face a similar dilemma in the slot this week, albeit on offense. Both Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams have been unable to practice, so if neither can go on Sunday, the Jets will have to make a change. One option could be to go with the guys currently on the roster. You could reactivate Jelani Woods and Tim Patrick and either run more multiple tight end packages, or use players like Garrett Wilson there. Another option could be to bring up Sterling Shepard or Jamaal Pritchett from the practice squad. The job share at running back remains a work in progress The Jets are still trying to figure out how to get the best out of Braelon Allen and Breece Hall now that both are healthy at the same time. Allen’s performances while Hall was out proved that he can benefit from a bigger workload. However, Hall brings different things to the table in the passing game, so the Jets will want him on the field more often than not. Last week was interesting because they employed Hall more in the passing game in the first half with Allen getting more carries. At the half, Allen had six carries and Hall had just two. However, after halftime, Allen carried the ball just twice and Hall had nine carries. It’s possible the Jets’ thinking was that Hall might produce better after halftime if he was fresh and the defense was tired. In the end, the pair had similar rushing numbers, but Hall produced more as a receiver. You can probably expect the Jets to keep working on this with one option being flipping last week’s gameplan on its head and using Hall early, then keeping Allen fresh to be the hammer in the second half. The Chargers’ run defense did a great job against the Ravens, holding them to 16 yards on 15 carries, so it might not be easy to get a running game established. Will Daiyan Henley play? The Chargers’ leading tackler is linebacker Daiyan Henley, but he’s been managing a knee issue all season and has been missing practice this week. Henley, who is also second on the team in defensive snaps played, has been exploited in coverage at times this year, but is still a key contributor to the Chargers’ run defense and tends to be the guy who wears the defensive headset. If Henley can’t go, the next man up would be Marlowe Wax, who has played under 100 defensive snaps in his career. Can the Jets get to Herbert? Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been struggling in the passing game. A large part of that is that the Chargers have struggled to protect him. Herbert has been sacked 33 times so far this season; more than every NFL quarterback apart from Deshaun Watson. Only two of their starting offensive linemen have started all nine games, which hasn’t helped matters. Last week, the Jets increased Will McDonald’s workload as they had promised to, but it meant that Kingsley Enagbare only got to rush the passer a season-low 15 times. With Joseph Ossai now also back in the rotation, sustaining McDonald’s level of opportunities might prove tricky. He did respond with a sack last week, though. Will New York be able to stop the run? The Jets’s run defense continues to struggle with two of their starting interior defensive linemen on injured reserve, although one – David Onyemata – was activated for practice this week, so is eligible to return. New York gave up over 200 yards to the Bills, including a back-breaking 74-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. The damage could have been even worse had it not been for the efforts of Harrison Phillips, though, as he stopped 10 runs for a gain of four or less. Los Angeles has the NFL’s worst scoring offense but they actually boast a top-10 running game and are coming off a game against the Ravens where Omarion Hampton rushed for over 100 yards for the first time all year. In addition, Herbert gave them a boost with a season-high 51 rushing yards, including his first touchdown. Can the Jets get the return game going? When the Jets won games last year, a feature of these performances was good production in the return game but that hasn’t been happening in 2026. If Williams is out this week, maybe that wouldn’t be the worst thing, because he’s been much less productive than last season. In last week’s game, the Jets used Isaiah Davis on kickoffs and he did quite well, having always put up solid numbers in the past. If Williams is out, then they may elevate someone like Pritchett to return punts, although the depth chart on the team’s official website lists Davis as the backup punt returner too. The bad news is that the Chargers’ coverage numbers are pretty solid, led by ex-Jets linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips who was the NFL’s leader in special teams tackles last season. On kickoffs, Cameron Dicker has allowed the third lowest return average in the NFL and their punter JK Scott is the number one graded punter according to Pro Football Focus rankings. Let us know how you see things going in Sunday’s game in the comments section

item.title: Confidence meters for Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current ahead of NWSL final
item.description: Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/NWSL via Getty Images | NWSL via Getty Images The NWSL playoffs are down to the last two standing: the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current. One team has rode their home-field advantage and will have another chance to play in front of their supporters, while the visitors have momentum from taking down the 2026 NWSL Shield winners. Which finalist heads into the final with more confidence and as the favorite? How confident should the NWSL finalists be? 1. Washington Spirit | Semifinals: 2-1 win vs Utah Royals *Quarterfinals: 4-1 win vs Portland Thorns Confidence meter: 65% Washington advanced to their third straight NWSL Championship final, but is this the year they finally break through? Is the third time actually the charm? First off, the ‘Rowdy’ Audi crowd is sure to provide an unmatched home-field advantage for Adrián González’s side who had the easier path in the bracket. In two playoff matches, Washington has generated an xG of 4.08 (six goals scored) while conceding just 1.81 xG (two goals allowed). Forward Clara Luvanga now has six goal contributions in her last four games (three goals and three assists). With the home crowd and the form they are in, this is their best chance to bring home the trophy. The only question left, can the Spirit finish the job? 2. Kansas City Current | Semfinals: 2-1 win at Gotham FC *Quarterfinals: 1-0 win vs Angel City FC Confidence meter: 35% Kansas City took down arguably the most in-form team in the quarterfinals in Angel City FC and followed it up by knocking out the best team from the regular season, Gotham FC. By taking down the Bats, Kansas City showed they can handle a difficult road atmosphere despite a 5-9-1 away record in the regular season. In two playoff matches, the Current have generated 2.92 xG (three goals scored), and conceded 1.79 xG (one goal allowed). The scary part? Scoring has come from Michelle Cooper, Croix Bethune and Haley Hopkins. Two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga is due for a huge goal and she might just bury the difference maker in the final. NWSL Championship final prediction Washington Spirit vs Kansas City Current | Saturday, November 21 at 8:00 p.m. ET on CBS/Paramount+ Winner: Washington Spirit

item.title: Arsenal is fighting Tottenham for Brazilian teenager
item.description: Arsenal is fighting Tottenham for Brazilian teenager Arthur Dias is regarded as one of the finest young talents in South American football as he continues to impress with Athletico Paranaense in the Brazilian top flight. The 19-year-old has attracted considerable attention with his performances and is expected to become a target for several European clubs in the coming seasons. Tottenham have been working hard to secure his signature, having identified him as one of the most promising talents available in the transfer market. The Lilywhites believe he has the potential to strengthen their squad in the future and are keen to bring him to Europe, where he could continue developing. However, they are now facing increased competition, with Arsenal entering the race to sign the Brazilian youngster. The Gunners are also keen to secure his services and could be in a strong position to challenge their London rivals. RTI Esporte reports that Mikel Arteta’s side have joined the list of clubs pursuing Dias, whom they regard as one of the standout talents in the Brazilian top flight. Arsenal have identified him as an ideal addition to their squad and are working hard to make a move happen. Arsenal step up their pursuit of Dias The Gunners believe Dias has the potential to become an important player in their squad and are determined to compete for his signature. Their interest represents a setback for Tottenham, who had previously appeared to be among the leading contenders for his services. Arsenal are reportedly in a stronger position than Spurs to complete the deal, which could give them an advantage in the race. Their ambition to recruit promising young players also makes Dias an attractive target as they look to strengthen their options for the future. (Photo by Ricardo Moreira/Getty Images) Brazilian connection could prove important Another factor that could work in Arsenal’s favour is the presence of an established Brazilian centre back in their squad. Having someone familiar with Brazilian football and its culture could help Dias settle more comfortably if he decides to move to north London. The opportunity to develop at Arsenal, alongside an established Brazilian defender, could be particularly appealing to the teenager. The Gunners will hope this connection helps convince him that their project offers the right environment for his development. Tottenham remain interested, but Arsenal’s involvement has made the competition for Dias considerably more challenging. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. Their interest represents a setback for Tottenham, who had previously appeared to be among the leading contenders for his services. Arsenal are reportedly in a stronger position than Spurs to complete the deal, which could give them an advantage in the race. Their ambition to recruit promising young players also makes Dias an attractive target as they look to strengthen their options for the future. (Photo by Ricardo Moreira/Getty Images) Brazilian connection could prove important Another factor that could work in Arsenal’s favour is the presence of an established Brazilian centre back in their squad. Having someone familiar with Brazilian football and its culture could help Dias settle more comfortably if he decides to move to north London. The opportunity to develop at Arsenal, alongside an established Brazilian defender, could be particularly appealing to the teenager. The Gunners will hope this connection helps convince him that their project offers the right environment for his development. Tottenham remain interested, but Arsenal’s involvement has made the competition for Dias considerably more challenging. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Colts Waive QB Daniel Jones: What It Means For Anthony Richardson Sr.
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 24: Anthony Richardson #5 of the Indianapolis Colts jumps in the air as he reacts during to an NFL preseason game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 24, 2023 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts have released quarterback Daniel Jones. It’s been a subpar season for both Jones and the Colts. The Colts are 3-8 and Jones ranks near the bottom of the barrel in multiple categories. Jones threw just seven touchdowns in 11 games with 13 interceptions. After a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday night with Jones completing just 12-of-27 passes for 144 yards and an interception, the Colts decided to make a major change. Jones, 29, signed a two-year extension with the Colts in March, with nearly $49.5 million of that guaranteed. With Jones now released, Colts head coach Shane Steichen announced that Anthony Richardson Sr. will start versus the New York Giants on Nov. 29. Anthony Richardson Gets Another Chance As Indianapolis Colts Starting QB Richardson was selected by the Colts with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, but his career has had ups and downs to this point. Richardson has thrown just six passes the last two seasons and has an 8-7 career starting record with 11 passing touchdowns, 13 interceptions and 10 rushing scores. Richardson is still just 24 years of age and there’s a chance his full potential has yet to be realized. With the Colts offensive line struggling, Richardson’s dual-threat capabilities could give the offense a boost. “I’m excited to see him play and go compete, and obviously he brings a unique skill set that’s very athletic and can run around and make some plays,” Steichen said . So, looking forward to seeing that.” Richardson is a free agent in March, and the Colts are a team that are in the midst of a rebuild and trying to figure out how they’ll look in 2027. The Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline and also traded offensive lineman Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. In short, the Colts have a largely depleted roster at the moment which is going to make it harder for the franchise and Richardson to succeed the rest of the season. Even if this isn’t the most ideal situation for Richardson to be thrust into as QB1, it’s better than no opportunity at all. If Richardson fares well, it’ll bode well for his future whether the Colts bring him back or he plays elsewhere next season. Steichen noted that Richardson has “matured a lot” between his rookie season and now and that a full week of practice reps as the starting quarterback will benefit him well. The Colts drafted him No. 4 overall in 2023 for a reason, and turning to Richardson once again as starting quarterback represents that they haven’t given up on his potential just yet. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Yankees 5-Player Trade Idea Dumps Anthony Volpe, Will Warren For Marlins Star
item.description: New York Yankees infielder Anthony Volpe The New York Yankees infield is a mess right now, and they may need to make a trade in order to fix it. Jazz Chisholm Jr. could be playing elsewhere next season. The Yankees have Anthony Volpe and Luis García Jr. as internal options to replace him, but they could look for better options. The Athletic's Jim Bowden proposed this trade that would net the Yankees Otto López from the Miami Marlins: Marlins receive: Jasson Domínguez, Anthony Volpe and Will Warren Yankees receive: Otto López and Agustín Ramírez López is a shortstop, but can also play second base. The Yankees could keep López at shortstop and move George Lombard Jr. to second base. Volpe would get a fresh start in Miami, playing next to Xavier Edwards. Ramírez would give the Yankees another option at catcher besides Wells. Another option for López on the Yankees would be playing third base to replace Ryan McMahon. The Yankees could then play García at second base, keeping him in the lineup regularly. As far as Domínguez and Warren go, the Yankees don't really need them. Warren is a solid pitcher, but the Yankees already have four All-Star-caliber starters. They have Cody Bellinger, Aaron Judge and Spencer Jones in the outfield, so Domínguez is expendable as well. The outfield and starting rotation are areas the Yankees can afford to deal from. López is under club control through 2029 and is coming off a season in which he was an All-Star and hit .305. More MLB: Over 12 Teams Reportedly Trying To Sign Freddy Peralta; Cubs, Padres, Rays Included

item.title: Bayern's Kane and Olise subbed out with injury
item.description: Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane receives treatment for an ankle injury on Friday (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Bayern Munich forwards Harry Kane and Michael Olise were subbed out after picking up injuries in the first-half of Friday's home Bundesliga clash with Cologne. With 15 minutes gone, England captain Kane was felled from behind by Cologne defender Joel Schmied in the box. After a VAR review, the referee waved away Kane's claims of a penalty. The Ballon d'Or winner tried to continue despite a clear limp, but was subbed out shortly after. Kane, 33, has a history of ankle complaints although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. Olise went down after a tackle near the penalty arc late in the first-half. Despite continuing until the break, the France player did not return to the pitch for the second-half. The former Crystal Palace winger left the stadium during the second-half on crutches for further treatment. Any potential further absences would come at a bad time for Bayern who are in the midst of an injury crisis, particularly up front. Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies and captain Manuel Neuer have all missed matches recently, while coach Vincent Kompany returned to the dugout on Friday after missing a month with a meningeal irritation. Bayern are the only team in Europe's top-five leagues yet to lose in any competition this season. They travel to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. dwi/ea

item.content:encoded: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - NOVEMBER 9: Chris Fields Jr. #2 of the Oakland Golden Grizzlies throws down a second half dunk against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Coleman Coliseum on November 9, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Brandon Sumrall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Game Information Game Time: 7 PM EST Location: Mackey Arena TV: Big 10 Network Oakland Golden Grizzlies (1-6) Conference: Horizon League Head Coach: Greg Kampe KenPom Rank: 209 Points Scored / Game: 70 (292) Points Allowed / Game: 88.4 (354) Best Win: 11/14 vs Northern Iowa (88-75) – KenPom 179 Worst Loss: 11/6 vs Stanford (81-63) – KenPom 86 Key Analytics Offense (per KenPom – National Rank in ()) Efficiency: 108.2 (146) Tempo: 68.1 (271) Effective Field Goal %: 46 (282) Offensive Rebound %: 37.7 (64) Turnover %: 20.4 (277) Two Point %: 48.2 (248) Three Point %: 28.4 (289) Key Analytics Defense (per KenPom – National Rank in ()) Efficiency: 112.8 (299) Effective Field Goal %: 59.9 (352) 3-Point %: 39.1 (337) 2-Point %: 61.2 (339) Key Players #2 – Chris Fields : Senior – Center – 6’8”, 240 – 17.9 Pts – 10.9 Reb – 1.3 Ast #0 – Nassim Mashhour: Junior – Wing – 6’6”, 200 – 17.9 Pts – 4 Reb – 2.1 Ast #6 – Ryder Bradley: Sophomore – Guard – 6’3”, 185 – 9.1 Pts – 2.6 Reb – 1.7 Ast Thoughts Oakland isn’t as bad as their 1-6 record or their stats/metrics indicate. They use their pre-conference slate to raise money via buy games against high-major teams. They’ve played the 8th-toughest schedule in the nation, with their only win coming in their lone home game against a similarly positioned mid-major. Basically, they’re losing basketball games on the road to fund their athletic department. I don’t see them as being much different than Valparaiso in terms of talent; in fact, Valparaiso is the perfect point of reference for Purdue fans. This team is built around two players: center Chris Fields and wing Nassim Mashhour. Valpo was built around two players: center JT Pettigrew and guard Rakim Chaney. The Boilermakers did a good job holding Pettigrew to 11 points (7 points below his season average) but couldn’t stop Rakim Chaney from going on a 35-point heater that will live on in Chaney family lore for generations. There’s no way Chaney wasn’t at the top of Purdue’s defensive game plan. The only way for the Beacons to come into the Mackey and leave with a victory was for their best player to do something exceptional, and yet, the Boilermaker defense looked surprised every time the ball went through the net. I’ve said this for multiple seasons, but I’m not sure I’ve ever seen a program so consistently bad at handling a hot player. If Purdue gets the ball out of Chaney’s hands, they win. I don’t understand why Coach Painter didn’t send an instant double and see if anyone else on the Beacons had the nerve to take big shots, but I digress. My point is that Oakland presents the exact same challenge. They have one interior player (Fields) and one perimeter player (Mashhour) who do the majority of their scoring. Mashhour is a balanced wing, shooting 37% from 3 and 42% from 2 while drawing 37 fouls and shooting 92% from the free-throw line. He’s the type of player who loves attack closeouts but won’t hesitate to pull the trigger from deep if the closeout is late. Remember, his early season stats are legit. He put up 15 last time out against Arizona State in his lowest-scoring game of the season. He put up 28 on Boise State, shooting 5/11 from deep and hitting all 9 of his free-throw attempts. The only way Purdue loses this game is if Mashhour goes nuclear, which is the same proposition they faced against Rakim Chaney. I’ll be interested to see if the coaching staff makes any adjustments to their defensive strategy tonight. With Mashhour taking care of things on the perimeter, Fields can focus his attention on the paint. He’s averaging a double-double against the 8th-toughest schedule in the nation. He went 17-for-11 against Arizona State, which included 8 free-throw attempts. He went 15-for-13 against Alabama, with another 7 free-throw attempts. I mention his free-throw attempts because he had the Sun Devils 7’1, 255-pound center Ben Defty tied to the bench with foul trouble all night. He played 17 minutes and fouled out trying to guard Fields in the post and keeping him off the boards. Defty’s backup, 6’11”, 200-pound Jonathan Grisham, played 11 minutes and committed 4 fouls. This will be a major challenge for Daniel Jacobsen on the defensive end. Fields will give him every opportunity to commit a foul, and as we all know, getting Jacobsen off the court is one of the keys to beating this Purdue team. I don’t think Oakland has enough to win this game, but I’ll be watching how this team handles the challenge they couldn’t navigate against Valpo. The task is clear. Stop Masshour and Fields, and short of a horrific shooting performance from the Boilermakers (which isn’t completely out of the question), Oakland won’t be able to generate enough offense to win. If one of these two goes off, and they’re both capable, things might be more uncomfortable than some folks are anticipating. Prediction KenPom Purdue – 83 Oakland – 64 Drew Purdue – 91 Oakland – 77 I’ve got the Boilermakers winning this game, but like the Lipscomb game, there may be a few uncomfortable moments before Purdue’s depth and overall talent advantage pull away late for a comfortable win. Antoine West wasn’t fully weaponized in the Valpo loss. He’ll keep Purdue out of danger with his scoring tonight.

item.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
item.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. Read full article Comments

item.title: Chelsea respond after being handed $196,000 fine by FA for anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chants
item.description: Chelsea have been hit with a fine by the FA -Credit:Lexy Ilsley, Manchester City FC via Getty Images Chelsea have been handed a £150,000 (over $196,200) fine by the FA following anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chanting from their supporters during an FA Cup match against Charlton Athletic in January. The Blues overcame the Championship club 5-1 at the Valley in the third-round fixture on January 10. The club has since been hit with a punishment and a warning from the FA, who have additionally imposed an action plan on the West London side. Chants heard in the 56th minute of the match were determined to be "improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way with either an express or implied reference to religion or belief", as per The Mirror . Tom Brady linked with Chelsea investment after abrupt Birmingham City exit U.S. Soccer executive opens up on search for Mauricio Pochettino replacement -Credit:Rob Newell - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images Chelsea accepted the charge but contested the fine, only for their appeal to be thrown out by an independent regulatory commission. The FA's written reasons acknowledged that while the chanting "lasted approximately one minute and was not repeated, the scale of participation was a significant aggravating feature". Chelsea responded with a statement: "We unequivocally condemn this behavior. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club. "Such behavior only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this. "Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behavior in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary. "Discriminatory behavior may constitute a criminal offense and supporters found to have breached the club's regulations will face disciplinary action, including possible match bans or membership suspensions. We will also require all those who may be sanctioned to take part in the Kick it Out programme as we believe education is as important as sanctions in order to root out this behavior for good. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. "We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. "We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward." The FA received a one-match ban, suspended for two years, alongside a £12,600 (just under $16,500) fine.

item.title: Sterling K. Brown in Talks to Star in New ‘Longlegs’ Movie with Nicolas Cage

item.title: Waste crisis: Acting LAWMA MD resumes, reads riot act to staff
item.description: .unveils 60-day action plan ​By Olasunkanmi Akoni Amid mounting concerns over waste management across the metropolis, the newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has assumed office with a stern warning to the workforce, reading the riot act against laxity. Akinyemi, also unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to clear backlogs and restore the agency’s past glory. ​Addressing management and staff at a tense workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s Ijora-Olopa headquarters on Friday, he made it clear that business as usual was over. Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi, the new helmsman demanded total commitment, positive work ethics, and renewed dedication to duty from every personnel, warning that repositioning the agency requires uncompromising discipline and active participation from all ranks. ​”We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. “We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi declared, signaling zero tolerance for operational inefficiencies. ​To back up his charge, Akinyemi rolled out a 60-day blueprint aimed at rapid waste evacuation, stricter regulatory enforcement, and aggressive field monitoring across Lagos State. While giving key highlights of the emergency plan, the MD boss said personnel will be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with local terrains to sharpen field monitoring and speed up response times. Hinting on decentralised operational hubs, Akinyemi added that the hubs will be established to decentralise waste management, tighten supervision, and bring rapid intervention closer to blackspots requiring urgent attention. On ​indiscriminate dumping, he avowed the agency’s determination to intensify community sensitization on waste sorting at source, mobilizing traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations, and artisans to enforce responsible disposal habits. Akinyemi, therefore, called for closer synergy with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and demanded stricter public compliance with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain operations. ​While reading the riot act on performance, the Acting MD also moved to boost morale, assuring workers that their welfare remains a top priority. He revealed ongoing efforts to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered staff buses to cushion transportation challenges. ​Earlier, Tijani, reiterated the call for urgency, promising an immediate overhaul and revitalisation of LAWMA’s operational framework to boost field performance. ​Similarly, Adebiyi, warned that the success of the 60-day plan hinges on prudent financial management, strict accountability, and synergy across all
