item.title: New NASA Seed Funding Primes Small Businesses for Innovation
item.description: Illustration of a future lunar vehicle that could potentially be powered by NASA-funded research, now under way, to develop an ultra-cold-tolerant battery module. Elementium Materials Inc. Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. This early-stage research and development work will tackle an array of topics, including those related to Artemis and the establishment of a U.S. Moon Base . Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies. Following are a few examples of research supported through these recent awards: Bringing Power to Moon and Mars An SBIR Phase II award for Opterus Research and Development Inc. supports a project focused on bringing power to the surface of the Moon and Mars by developing a modular system of rollable solar arrays. The arrays can be handled robotically, are compatible with various support structures, and work even in dusty surface conditions. The technology could be scaled up to 50 kilowatts, and it could provide a reliable power source to help both NASA and commercial space companies develop infrastructure on the Moon . Rovers With Reach: Vision and Tactile Sensing in Robotic Arm This SBIR Phase I award, led by Intelligent Fiber Optic Systems Corporation, aims to help lunar rovers perform complex tasks independently on the Moon. The firm’s 10-foot, extendable robotic arm can both “see” and has a sense of touch, combining a camera with sensors to detect and measure surface textures, contact forces, and temperature. item.dc:creator: Abby Tabor
item.content:encoded: Illustration of a future lunar vehicle that could potentially be powered by NASA-funded research, now under way, to develop an ultra-cold-tolerant battery module. Elementium Materials Inc. Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. This early-stage research and development work will tackle an array of topics, including those related to Artemis and the establishment of a U.S. Moon Base . Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies. Following are a few examples of research supported through these recent awards: Bringing Power to Moon and Mars An SBIR Phase II award for Opterus Research and Development Inc. supports a project focused on bringing power to the surface of the Moon and Mars by developing a modular system of rollable solar arrays. The arrays can be handled robotically, are compatible with various support structures, and work even in dusty surface conditions. The technology could be scaled up to 50 kilowatts, and it could provide a reliable power source to help both NASA and commercial space companies develop infrastructure on the Moon . Rovers With Reach: Vision and Tactile Sensing in Robotic Arm This SBIR Phase I award, led by Intelligent Fiber Optic Systems Corporation, aims to help lunar rovers perform complex tasks independently on the Moon. The firm’s 10-foot, extendable robotic arm can both “see” and has a sense of touch, combining a camera with sensors to detect and measure surface textures, contact forces, and temperature. The technology could help automate many lunar surface tasks, such as cleaning solar panels, positioning habitat structures, and collecting scientific samples from hard-to-reach locations. On Earth, the same instrumented robotic arms could be used to inspect and repair power lines, nuclear reactors, or other infrastructure in hazardous environments. Cold-Friendly Battery for Long Lunar Night Elementium Materials Inc., selected for an SBIR Phase I award, is developing an ultra-cold-tolerant battery module for space applications and cold-climate uses on Earth. The technology can operate down to minus 76 degrees Fahrenheit without active heating, reducing the need for heaters and insulating layers to work on the Moon. With the space and mass that’s saved, NASA missions can launch other tools and science experiments, instead. This battery technology could help keep rovers, habitats, and other infrastructure running through the frigid, 14-day lunar night and potentially on Mars. Prepare for Landing — Repeatedly — on Moon A collaboration between Slate Geotechnical Consultants Inc. and the Colorado School of Mines will evaluate two approaches to preparing lunar regolith for repeated lunar landings, so that routine mission activities can have sturdy, reusable landing pads. Without such pads, the force generated by a rocket can blast out loose, gravel-like regolith from the surface, throw up dust, or create craters, potentially damaging spacecraft and nearby infrastructure. The project, supported by an STTR Phase I award, will also investigate ways to use rovers to repair and maintain future lunar landing pads. Complete lists of the selected proposals are available on the SBIR/STTR program’s website: Phase I: 2026 NASA SBIR Appendix A Phase I 2026 NASA SBIR Appendix B Phase I 2026 NASA STTR Appendix B Phase I Phase II: 2025 NASA SBIR Phase II NASA’s SBIR/STTR program is part of the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate and is managed by NASA’s Ames Research Center in California’s Silicon Valley.

item.title: I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2. Watch the video below. ﻿ The post I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello appeared first on Channels Television .

item.description: YouTube is preparing to pay $3 billion to thousands of school districts to settle claims that its "addictive design" harmed kids, according to Bloomberg . item.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
item.description: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post . "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private. Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." Apple is taking some action to implement protection from AI agents on macOS, though it appears to be doing so largely to defend against third-party access to data rather than to limit its own Siri service. Siri can be turned off separately. With macOS 27.3 , currently in public beta testing, Apple's desktop operating system will get more granular controls on two APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. The result will be more permission prompts for users of macOS apps that seek access to user data, and the inconvenience of applying for an entitlement from Apple to obtain Full Disk Access for backup software and assistive technologies that use Accessibility APIs. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private. Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." Apple is taking some action to implement protection from AI agents on macOS, though it appears to be doing so largely to defend against third-party access to data rather than to limit its own Siri service. Siri can be turned off separately. With macOS 27.3 , currently in public beta testing, Apple's desktop operating system will get more granular controls on two APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. The result will be more permission prompts for users of macOS apps that seek access to user data, and the inconvenience of applying for an entitlement from Apple to obtain Full Disk Access for backup software and assistive technologies that use Accessibility APIs. "As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially," Apple said when it introduced the Full Disk Access change. "We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy." Apple is also reportedly working on its own AI agent in a bid to compete with Anthropic and OpenAI. It remains to be seen whether Apple will use its operating system ownership as competitive leverage against AI firms that threaten its gatekeeping power, as it has done with web browsers . First the flood, then the dams While Apple casts itself as an ally that's helping to defend device customers against prying AI agents, Signal's decision to block Siri shows that AI agents have complicated trust decisions and the competitive landscape. AI agents are supposed to serve the user but when they spirit data away to the cloud and come between customers and merchants, they wear out their welcome. AI agents also threaten the business relationship between consumers and merchants. Amazon has blocked shopping agents like Meta Muse from its e-commerce site (though not AWS Marketplace ) while Walmart has invited third-party agents to interact through its AI Gateway. Anthropic has blocked subscription customers from using third-party harnesses . United Airlines has banned transactions from unauthorized AI bots. Similar barriers or limitations related to third-party AI agents have been erected by Target, Home Depot, Etsy, eBay, JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo, among others. Meanwhile, there's a burgeoning industry in bot detection and mitigation, led by the likes of Cloudflare, Akamai, and DataDome, to name a few. The web browser is sometimes referred to as a user agent, based on the idealistic notion that it serves its user. That vision has been muddied by online advertising and data collection, and default settings that often serve the interests of browser makers instead of promoting privacy. Now AI agents face the same scrutiny as people wonder whether their agents really serve them or someone else. After a year or two of agent vendors arguing for access to all digital data for the sake of personalization and context, the backlash has arrived. ®

item.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
item.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain
item.description: SpaceX's successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA's path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-important, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year. For SpaceX's purposes, Saturday's mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX's deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon. Early next year, SpaceX plans to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX's existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. With two launch sites, SpaceX will have the pieces in place to take the next leap with Starship. Read full article Comments

item.content:encoded: SpaceX's successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA's path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-important, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year. For SpaceX's purposes, Saturday's mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX's deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon. Early next year, SpaceX plans to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX's existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. item.title: Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO
item.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday. The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday. The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said that the incident was not a system collapse. It said that the disturbance resulted from the tripping of some transmission line, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”NISO wishes to clarify that the grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse. “It resulted from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”At 12:34 p.m., the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex. ”Subsequently, at 12:50 p.m, the Ihovbor–Oshogbo transmission line tripped alongside the Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in load losses in some parts of the country,” it said. The system operator said that prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilize the grid and restore affected transmission lines. It said that all the affected lines had since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49 p.m. on Friday. It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations, and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid. ”The public is advised to rely on official communications from NISO for accurate information on developments within the national electricity grid,” it said. (NAN) The post Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Afenifere demands prosecution of sponsors of campaign violence
item.description: …Raises alarm over rising attacks ahead of 2027 elections By Adeola Badru The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has raised the alarm over increasing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling for the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators and their sponsors. The organisation warned that the growing incidents of thuggery, intimidation and inflammatory political rhetoric posed a serious threat to the country’s democratic process. Afenifere, in a statement issued on Friday by its National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, called on political parties, candidates, their sponsors and supporters to end violence and ensure that campaigns were conducted in accordance with the Constitution and the Electoral Act. Ajayi expressed concern over reported attacks on political figures, campaign convoys and supporters in different parts of the country, warning that the growing atmosphere of hostility could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and endanger lives. Among the incidents cited was the reported attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu on Friday, November 13, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Central Mosque, Abuja. According to the organisation, assailants threw stones and other dangerous objects at the departing presidential convoy, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: …Raises alarm over rising attacks ahead of 2027 elections By Adeola Badru The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has raised the alarm over increasing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling for the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators and their sponsors. The organisation warned that the growing incidents of thuggery, intimidation and inflammatory political rhetoric posed a serious threat to the country’s democratic process. Afenifere, in a statement issued on Friday by its National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, called on political parties, candidates, their sponsors and supporters to end violence and ensure that campaigns were conducted in accordance with the Constitution and the Electoral Act. Ajayi expressed concern over reported attacks on political figures, campaign convoys and supporters in different parts of the country, warning that the growing atmosphere of hostility could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and endanger lives. Among the incidents cited was the reported attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu on Friday, November 13, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Central Mosque, Abuja. According to the organisation, assailants threw stones and other dangerous objects at the departing presidential convoy, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives. Afenifere also condemned the attack on supporters of the Accord Party governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, around the Molete area of Ibadan, which reportedly resulted in the death of a 40-year-old supporter, Azeez Tajudeen. It described the incident as particularly disturbing, saying the destruction of vehicles and loss of life highlighted the consequences of allowing political differences to degenerate into violence. The organisation further listed the reported attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State; the reported assault on the convoy of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Calabar, Cross River State; and disruptions of political gatherings, particularly those of the APC and ADC in Sokoto, Kebbi and Lagos states. It said the incidents reflected a disturbing pattern requiring urgent intervention by political leaders and security agencies. Ajayi also recalled the warning by former President Goodluck Jonathan at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Peace Conference in Abuja, where he cautioned political leaders against running their parties like rival cult groups. Jonathan had warned against recruiting and exploiting young Nigerians for political violence, saying such practices could plunge the country into avoidable crises. Similarly, Senate President Godswill Akpabio had cautioned youths against allowing themselves to be used for political violence, warning that perpetrators could face serious criminal charges, including treasonable felony. Afenifere also referenced concerns raised by former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, and the National Peace Committee’s Co-convener, Most Rev. Matthew Kukah, over inflammatory political campaigns. The interventions, it noted, followed reports of about 60 election-related incidents across the country within a month. The organisation also recalled President Tinubu’s directive condemning political violence across party lines and insisting that the 2027 elections should be defined by ideas rather than hostility. Highlighting the legal implications of electoral violence, Afenifere reminded political parties, candidates and their sponsors that recruiting, organising or financing political thugs constituted a criminal offence under Nigerian law. It cited Section 227 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which prohibits political parties and associations from retaining, organising, training or equipping individuals or groups to use physical force or coercion in promoting political objectives. It also referenced Section 78 of the Electoral Act, which, according to the organisation, prescribes fines of N5 million for a first offence and N7 million for subsequent offences by political parties, as well as N500,000 for every day the offence continues. Individuals or groups who aid or abet such violations could also face a fine of N5 million, imprisonment for five years or both, it said. Ajayi further cited Sections 92 and 93 of the Electoral Act, which criminalise political thuggery and the direct or indirect use or threat of force during election campaigns. He said offenders could face up to 12 months’ imprisonment or a fine of N1 million, while political parties found culpable could also incur financial penalties. “The provisions of the laws are quite clear. But impunity persists because sponsors of violence are rarely brought to book,” Ajayi said. He urged political leaders to call their supporters to order, stressing that those seeking political offices had a responsibility to ensure peaceful campaigns. The Afenifere spokesman also appealed to Nigerian youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of violence by politicians. “Nigerian youths must refuse to be used as cannon fodders by desperate politicians whose own children are safely tucked away from harm,” he warned. He urged political actors to respect the President’s position that the 2027 elections should be a democratic contest characterised by the exchange of ideas, peaceful participation and respect for the rights of Nigerians. Afenifere further called on stakeholders to ensure that political parties and candidates enjoyed equal protection and freedom to campaign in every part of the country without harassment, intimidation or threats to their safety. The organisation specifically challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the Nigeria Police Force and the judiciary to move beyond public condemnations and take concrete action against electoral violence. It demanded the prompt arrest and prosecution of those responsible for attacks, including individuals and groups financing or sponsoring them, as well as the disqualification of offenders where permitted by law. Afenifere insisted that accountability should not end with the arrest of foot soldiers, but must extend to those who finance, organise and deploy political thugs. It warned that failure to decisively address political violence could undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections and threaten Nigeria’s democratic stability beyond the polls. The post Afenifere demands prosecution of sponsors of campaign violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Obi woos Onitsha voters, promises jobs, better services
item.description: …Says Nigeria needs energetic president By Vincent Ujumadu The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday drew a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall meeting in the commercial city. Obi began his visit with a stop at his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he told students that the institution had produced three state governors and could soon produce Nigeria’s president. The three former governors he identified were Peter Odili of Rivers State, Obi himself and Willie Obiano, who succeeded him as governor of Anambra State. Addressing the students, Obi promised to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in the 2027 general elections. His campaign train subsequently moved through Oguta Road, Upper Iweka, Head Bridge, Uga Road and Modebe Avenue before arriving at All Saints Cathedral, venue of the town hall meeting. Among those who accompanied him during the roadshow were Aisha Yesufu and other members of his campaign team. Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign music, while several traders reportedly closed their shops to attend the town hall meeting. Addressing supporters at the gathering, Obi said he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, had formed a team committed to uniting the country, tackling insecurity and corruption, and ensuring that public resources were used for the benefit of Nigerians. “Kwankwaso and I have formed a team that will unite and secure Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, fight corruption and use public money for public good. “I assure Nigerians that from day one, they will be feeling the good impact of their country. You will know that a new team is in charge,” he said. He promised to move Nigeria from a consumption-driven economy to one centred on production, create employment opportunities and invest in critical sectors. “We cannot continue with the present situation where our children don’t have jobs because that is not the way a country should be,” he said. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: …Says Nigeria needs energetic president By Vincent Ujumadu The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday drew a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall meeting in the commercial city. Obi began his visit with a stop at his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he told students that the institution had produced three state governors and could soon produce Nigeria’s president. The three former governors he identified were Peter Odili of Rivers State, Obi himself and Willie Obiano, who succeeded him as governor of Anambra State. Addressing the students, Obi promised to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in the 2027 general elections. His campaign train subsequently moved through Oguta Road, Upper Iweka, Head Bridge, Uga Road and Modebe Avenue before arriving at All Saints Cathedral, venue of the town hall meeting. Among those who accompanied him during the roadshow were Aisha Yesufu and other members of his campaign team. Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign music, while several traders reportedly closed their shops to attend the town hall meeting. Addressing supporters at the gathering, Obi said he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, had formed a team committed to uniting the country, tackling insecurity and corruption, and ensuring that public resources were used for the benefit of Nigerians. “Kwankwaso and I have formed a team that will unite and secure Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, fight corruption and use public money for public good. “I assure Nigerians that from day one, they will be feeling the good impact of their country. You will know that a new team is in charge,” he said. He promised to move Nigeria from a consumption-driven economy to one centred on production, create employment opportunities and invest in critical sectors. “We cannot continue with the present situation where our children don’t have jobs because that is not the way a country should be,” he said. On healthcare, Obi advocated a system where Nigerians could access functional medical facilities without having to depend on religious institutions for treatment. He pledged to establish functional primary healthcare centres in every ward and said his proposed administration would build 10,000 healthcare centres across the country. He also promised that his administration would commence the construction of 40,000 classroom blocks from its first day in office, alongside increased investment in education and healthcare. On electricity, the former Anambra governor expressed concern over Nigeria’s power generation capacity, which he put at about 5,000 megawatts. He said his proposed administration would work towards generating, transmitting and distributing 10,000 megawatts of electricity. Obi urged Nigerians to hold him and his running mate accountable for their campaign promises, insisting that they were not making promises without understanding the country’s challenges. “We don’t want to make false promises. We are not going to tell Nigerians what we saw when we came in. We are seeing everything now and we are planning for it,” he said. He also urged voters to actively participate in the 2027 elections and protect their votes by remaining at polling units until votes were counted and results transmitted. “I want all of you to know that you are contestants in the forthcoming elections, although you are doing it through those of us that are candidates. So, on that day, sacrifice it for Nigeria,” he told the gathering. He urged voters to remain at their polling units after casting their ballots, adding that they should not be intimidated into leaving before the conclusion of the counting and result-transmission processes. Obi also called on supporters to vote for NDC candidates in the presidential, senatorial and House of Representatives elections, as well as the subsequent House of Assembly election. On the economy, he criticised the Federal Government’s handling of the removal of petrol subsidy, arguing that the policy had contributed to rising living costs and worsening hardship. He also questioned the government’s borrowing, alleging that it had accumulated more debt than previous administrations combined, while raising concerns about the implementation of successive national budgets. “Today, he has borrowed more money than all the previous governments put together. The question is, where is our money?” he asked. Obi called for a change of government in 2027, saying Nigeria needed leadership defined by competence, compassion, commitment and character. He also questioned President Bola Tinubu’s capacity to sustain the demands of the presidency, arguing that the country needed an energetic leader. “Above all, we want a government that has energy. Our current president has to go and rest because he is tired. This job requires energy and the person doing it must have energy. That is why we are begging him to go and rest,” he said. item.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
item.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns
item.dc:creator: Fran Ruiz
item.content:encoded: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns with alien NPCs, gigantic kaiju-like beasts, and... fishing . The endless free updates have pushed the roleplaying aspects deeper, as Hello Games are really making it the "forever" space game. Most importantly though, you can be the greatest bad guy the virtually infinite universe has ever seen, controlling entire pirate fleets and firing on (or stealing) every spaceship that you come across. It might be a bit aimless for some, but if you love a "forever game" then NMS can be the biggest space-set criminal sim ever created. Star Wars almost got it right (Image credit: Ubisoft) Though it took too long, Star Wars has gotten really close to cracking the GTA formula in outer space in a shameless enough way. 2024's Star Wars Outlaws is, to this date, the closest thing we've received to a space-set sandbox directly inspired by Rockstar's huge hits. By letting us fully embrace the Han Solo-like scoundrel fantasy, Massive Entertainment delivered a Star Wars adventure that's all about breaking the law. Hell, they even got a wanted system in there that has protagonist Kay Vess dodging stormtroopers and rival criminal factions like you would in Vice City. Star Wars Outlaws' take on GTA isn't just about the surface-level gameplay and open structure; it also understands much of its playful tone, moral ambiguity, and stressful rhythm. Jumping between several medium-sized maps set on different planets and spaceship sections breaks up the experience a little, so it never quite reaches that level of seamless immersion, but if anyone wants to do a focused version of GTA in space in the future, Massive's attempt is the one game that got at least halfway there. The ones we lost (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Before we go (and before you go back to playing GTA VI), we should remember the daring video games that, for a variety of reasons, never got to realize their visions of a crime-oriented space adventure. Remember Star Wars 1313 and Visceral Games' cancelled project ? It's hard not to spot some of their DNA surviving in Outlaws. As Luke Skywalker wisely said before noping out, "No one's ever really gone." Lucasfilm loves that, and it extends to binned video games too, thankfully. Even the elusive Battlefront 3 is back from the dead now. Bethesda also had something going at some point with "Prey 2", a bounty hunter action game set in a cyberpunk-ish alien world. Before it was canned, it dropped one of the coolest CG game trailers ever made and teased us with a Blade Runner-esque future long before Cyberpunk hit our consoles. (Image credit: Ubisoft) Looking at the future, Ubisoft's Beyond Good & Evil 2 wants to go big and lawless, potentially iterating on Star Wars Outlaws and other open-world crime sims. But years after its announcement and many mind-boggling development news updates, it's hard to believe it's really ever coming out. Maybe the "Before GTA VI" meme can morph into "Before BG&E2" now that Rockstar's masterpiece is finally out. Ultimately, Rockstar is Rockstar. A one-of-a-kind megastudio with nearly unlimited resources. Trying to replicate GTA does — either on Earth or among the stars — would be an Icarus flight in the making for most studios. There are some GTA-flavored space adventures out there, as we've shown, but we're still waiting for the one. Something that matches the deep storytelling, complete freedom, and cheeky tone of Rockstar's iconic series. OK, I gotta get out of here, I'm too hip for this, I gotta play GTA VI some more. Grand Theft Auto VI: $79.99 Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. item.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
item.description: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’ve done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday. In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

item.title: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons. Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing : The pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts. CTIA said the pilot test shows "that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications." Read full article Comments

item.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
item.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. item.content:encoded: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. On data protection, Oyedele called on financial institutions to strengthen safeguards around customers’ personal and financial information to protect them against fraud and other abuses. He said public confidence in the financial system depended on customers being assured that their money was safe, their information was handled responsibly and the terms of financial products were clearly explained. He also stressed the importance of customer education on protecting account credentials, identifying suspicious messages and reporting suspected fraud. According to him, financial institutions must provide accessible complaint-resolution channels and ensure customers know who is handling their complaints and when to expect a response. He said cooperation between financial institutions and regulators remained essential to sustaining confidence in the financial system as digital financial services expanded. Oyedele commended Moniepoint for establishing its Abuja office, noting that the Federal Capital Territory provided a strategic location for serving businesses and communities across the North-Central and Northern regions. “The location of this hub is significant. Abuja connects important commercial routes and provides a base for serving communities across North-Central and Northern Nigeria, including areas with substantial agricultural potential,” he said. In his remarks, the Chief Executive Officer of Moniepoint, Tunde Olofin, described the financial institution as a bank of choice, attributing its growth to its digital banking services and innovative products. He listed instant settlement for businesses and working capital loans among the products that had strengthened the bank’s appeal to customers. Olofin said the opening of the Abuja branch marked an expansion of the bank’s services beyond digital channels, providing customers with physical locations where they could receive face-to-face support and interact with business relationship managers. He said the bank planned to establish more branches in additional states to bring its services closer to customers. Olofin reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to building what he described as financial happiness for every Nigerian. Also speaking, the Managing Director of Shared Agent Network Expansion Facilities (SANEF) Limited, Uche Uzoebo, commended Moniepoint’s innovation and urged young Nigerians to contribute to national development. She said Nigerians must take responsibility for building the country rather than expecting others to do so. “I want to tell us Nigerians that we have to believe in ourselves. If we don’t build this place, nobody will build Nigeria for us,” she said. The post Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
item.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." item.content:encoded: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." Artist's illustration of NASA's Mars Odyssey orbiter circling the Red Planet. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Mars Odyssey loses another reaction wheel Mars Odyssey's problem may be more serious: The orbiter, which arrived at the Red Planet in October 2001, recently lost the use of one of its reaction wheels. Odyssey has four reaction wheels, which help the spacecraft maintain its orientation in space. Three of the four must be functional to do this job, and Odyssey already lost a reaction wheel in 2013. This latest issue cropped up on Nov. 4, when Odyssey went into safe mode. The orbiter stayed in this protective posture until Nov. 6 while mission team members diagnosed and dealt with the problem. They've made some progress, at one point getting the faulty wheel to move when commanded. "Further testing is being conducted to confirm whether the wheel is recoverable," NASA officials wrote in Thursday's update. Though it has been out of safe mode for two weeks, Odyssey still has not resumed its science or data-relay work. (The orbiter has long helped NASA's Mars surface craft send information home to Earth.) "The goal is for Odyssey to return to science and relay operations at the conclusion of these tests and analysis during the last week of November, and NASA will provide future updates on status and timeline as the team learns more," agency officials wrote in the update. If the reaction wheel, isn't recoverable, Odyssey's days are numbered. The mission team will have to orient the orbiter solely using its thrusters, and Odyssey has enough hydrazine fuel left to do this for a just month or two, according to NASA. Odyssey's mission has been a rousing success, no matter what happens with the reaction wheel. The orbiter has operated at Mars longer than any other spacecraft, and it has made a number of important scientific contributions. "Odyssey created the first global maps detailing the composition of the Martian surface, which have become foundational for Mars geologists," NASA officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The orbiter's surface maps have also played a key role in identifying hazards at landing sites, spotting locations of scientific interest for landers and rovers to explore, and mapping water molecules in the top 3 feet (1 meter) of the surface, including buried ice that could be useful to the first astronauts on Mars ."

item.title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
item.description: …Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said. item.title: ‘I won’t disappoint you in my second term’ – Adeleke assures Osun people
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration. A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying. Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy. According to him, the Osun election that re-elected Governor Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it. “That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people,” he submitted on behalf of the Chief Imam of Osogboland, Sheikh Musa Animasahun. The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Hon. Teslim Igbalaye; Osun Central Accord Senatorial candidate, Hon. Ganiyu Olaoluwa; members of the state executive council; special advisers; and top government functionaries. The post ‘I won’t disappoint you in my second term’ – Adeleke assures Osun people appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Army delays detonating "catastrophically hazardous" lead azide amid fear, anger
item.description: In a swirl of questions, fears, and outrage, the US Army announced late Thursday that it would delay a plan to blow up 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide, which would launch toxic gas and lead into the air. The plume, containing neurotoxic lead, could potentially drift 100 miles north of the Army installation housing it in Middletown, Iowa, according to modeling released by the Army earlier this week. The Army had planned to carry out two controlled detonations, set off simultaneously around noon Friday, to destroy the barrels where they lie, which is in earth-covered concrete containment structures (called earth-covered magazines or ECMs). Now the Army plans to wait until November 23 to provide more time to communicate about the situation with Iowans, who have reported being unaware of the detonations until earlier this week. "Public communication is essential to public trust," Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said in a post on social media at 7:31 pm ET Thursday . "Therefore, the Army will continue to actively engage with state and local officials throughout the region to distribute accurate, up-to-date information." Read full article Comments

item.title: UNICEF, Lagos raise alarm over threats to children’s rights
item.description: …As children demand free education, protection, greater say in policies By Chioma Obinna The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have called for stronger protection of children’s rights, warning that their welfare and fundamental rights are increasingly under threat and require concrete government action. The call was made on Friday during the commemoration of the 2026 World Children’s Day at the UNICEF Lagos Office, with the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.” UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, said children’s rights were facing growing threats globally, stressing the need for governments and other stakeholders to guarantee every child access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to all, particularly the most vulnerable. She emphasised the importance of social protection programmes, noting that the existence of rights did not automatically translate into access to basic necessities. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said, explaining that social protection interventions could help vulnerable children access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. She added that Nigeria’s future depended largely on the attention and investment devoted to children today. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” Lafoucriere declared. The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that it could not achieve the objective without the support of other stakeholders. He urged parents, schools, communities, development partners and other stakeholders to work together to create an environment where every child felt safe, valued and heard. “We must translate what we hear today into meaningful action and commitment,” he said. Ogunlende assured the children that their contributions and concerns raised during the celebration would not end with the event but would inform government policies and practical interventions. Also speaking, the Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their lives, insisting that their voices must be considered in the formulation of policies concerning them. He said children were better positioned to communicate their experiences, particularly in cases involving abuse and other challenges.
