item.dc:creator: Ahmad Adedimeji Amobi
item.content:encoded: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success. A closer look at the nominations across the four editions reveals just how much Nigerian music has featured in the category. In 2024, four of the five nominated recordings featured Nigerian artists. The following year, all five recordings had Nigerian representation, with seven Nigerian artists making the list. In 2026, three of the five recordings featured Nigerian artists, while the 2027 nominations saw four out of five recordings feature at least one Nigerian artist. Altogether, Nigerian artists have featured in 16 of the 20 nominated recordings since the category was introduced. This is not to suggest that Nigerian music does not deserve the recognition it receives. Nigerian artists have built impressive international careers, and their music has found audiences far beyond the continent. They deserve to be recognised. However, when a category is created to recognise the best of African music, it is worth asking how much of the continent’s musical diversity is reflected in its nominations. In September 2024, Tyla made a similar observation when she won the Best Afrobeats award at the MTV Video Music Awards. In her acceptance speech, she said, “There is a tendency to group all African artists under Afrobeats… Even though Afrobeats has run things and has opened so many doors for us, African music is so diverse. It is more than just Afrobeats.” Africa has a vast and diverse music industry. From South Africa’s Amapiano movement and Ghana’s Highlife and Hiplife traditions to Uganda’s dance music, Tanzania’s Bongo Flava and the different sounds emerging from Francophone Africa, there is no shortage of music deserving of international attention. The prominence of Nigerian artists in this category may partly reflect the strength of the country’s music industry and the international visibility its artists have built over the years. It may also reflect the Recording Academy’s membership, voting processes and the music that reaches its voters. But that is precisely why the conversation is important. If the category is to represent African music, its nominations should encourage listeners to discover artists and sounds beyond the ones they already know. Nigerian music has benefited from a relatively strong music industry, with established record labels, international distribution deals, collaborations with global artists and a large diaspora audience that continues to support its exports. These factors have helped Nigerian artists reach international audiences and, by extension, become more visible to institutions such as the Recording Academy. However, this visibility does not necessarily mean that the best or most interesting music coming out of Africa is always the music that gets heard internationally. An artist from another African country may be producing equally compelling music but lack the distribution network, marketing resources or international connections to get it beyond their local market. If the music awards are interested in recognising the best of African music, perhaps there is also a need to look beyond the music that already has an established international audience. After all, one of the things an award can do is introduce the world to music it might otherwise never discover. There is a difference between recognising the best of African music and repeatedly recognising only the most internationally visible parts of it. The Best African Music Performance has opened an important door for African music. The next step is ensuring that more of the continent gets to walk through it. The post Are Nigerian Artists Dominating the Grammys’ Best African Music Performance Category? appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
item.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.” Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...

item.title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid
item.description: ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2 . The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before. The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards. Continue reading...

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
item.description: null On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there. (Image credit: SETI) Why it mattered The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute. "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's." The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University . The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI. As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13. The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also b eamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Relive Starship's historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and 'Mechazilla' tower catch
item.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase. It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable. Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did. The 33 Raptor engines of SpaceX's Starship V3 rocket during its test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench. Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies. Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II , with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away. EOS R5 Mark II: $3999 This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling. Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review . View Deal Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas, as a bird passes on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space , while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase. Super Heavy (top) performs a boostback burn after stage separation as Ship 42 (bottom) fires its engines on its way to space. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) That return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase. Super Heavy descends back toward Texas on Nov.
item.dc:creator: Josh Dinner
item.content:encoded: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase. It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable. Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did. The 33 Raptor engines of SpaceX's Starship V3 rocket during its test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench. Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies. Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II , with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away. EOS R5 Mark II: $3999 This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling. Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review . View Deal Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas, as a bird passes on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space , while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase. Super Heavy (top) performs a boostback burn after stage separation as Ship 42 (bottom) fires its engines on its way to space. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) That return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase. Super Heavy descends back toward Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Super Heavy flies back toward Texas, firing its engines to slow its descnet on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Super heavy performed its landing burn above the Gulf of Mexico before cutting its engines for a brief moment and exploding in a giant fireball. Super Heavy flies back toward Texas, firing its engines to slow its descnet on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) This was an intentional detonation, courtesy of the vehicle's flight termination system. Three-panel image showing Super Heavy's landing burn, engine cutoff and subsequent explosion. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) Ship continued on to low Earth orbit , where it deployed a payload of 26 upgraded Starlink Version 3 satellites . It was the second batch of V3 Starlinks delivered during Starship’s recent flight tests, each of which has added what SpaceX says is the equivalent of 10 Falcon 9 Starlink V2 satellite launches worth of data capacity to its orbital constellation. Flight 15 was also Starship's second-ever mission to orbit, and its longest so far. Ship spent nearly a full day in orbit, circling Earth a total of 14 times. During its jaunt in space, the spacecraft cleared three separate check points, which allowed SpaceX the opportunity to divert the vehicle for an ocean splashdown if needed, and finally was given the green light to attempt the first-ever Ship tower catch. SpaceX's Starship V3 rocket launches on a test flight from Starbase, Texas on May 22, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) At approximately 4:18 p.m. EST (2018 GMT, 3:18 p.m. local time in Texas) on Saturday (Nov. 14), the spacecraft broke through the cloud cover that blanketed the skies above Starbase as onlookers watched its bellyflop plunge toward the ground. Moments after becoming visible, Ship ignited its engines for a flip and burn maneuver, which oriented it upright and swung its trajectory into the tightening grip of the chopstick arms of Starbase's "Mechazilla" launch tower. Starship upper stage approaches the launch tower in Starbase, Texas on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) After a slight sway back and forth suspended above Earth in Mechazilla's embrace, Ship came to a complete rest, hanging motionless as a historic milestone in SpaceX’s pursuit of fully reusable spaceflight. Starship upper stage lowers into the launch tower in Starbase, Texas on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) The six Raptor 3 engines that powered Ship 42's return are seen as the vehicle hangs by the arms of the "Mechazilla" launch tower arms. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) It hung there overnight as engineers, and even SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , inspected the spacecraft. Ship was lowered on Sunday (Nov. 15) and transported back to SpaceX's Starbase hanger bay for further checkouts. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) SpaceX has not yet said whether Ship 42 will fly again, but its return gives engineers a chance to examine how the spacecraft held up through launch, nearly a day in orbit and atmospheric reentry. Starship hangs, caught by its launch tower on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Those findings will help inform upcoming flights as SpaceX ramps up production to continue testing Starship's capabilities. Starship hangs, caught by its launch tower on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner)

item.title: This Week’s Playlist Update Comes With Wande Coal, Seyi Shay, Olamide, Khaid & More
item.description: Seyi Shay teams up with French artist Vegedream on her new single “Love & War”, one of the standout releases in this week’s music roundup. Photo Credit: Instagram A fresh Monday means it is time to clear out last week’s queue and make room for the sounds shaping Nigerian music right now. From Wande Coal reuniting with Juls and Patoranking linking up with Olamide for a musical salute to Lagos, to Khaid bridging generations with Fuji legend Saheed Osupa , Spyro delivering a quick dancefloor starter, and Seyi Shay trading English and French verses with Vegedream , there is plenty to keep your headphones busy over the next few days. Wande Coal – “Kowope” Kicking things off is Wande Coal , who reunites with British-Ghanaian producer Juls on “Kowope”, marking their first collaboration since the hit “So Mi So”. The new single is also Wande Coal’s first solo release since he put out his 15-track album KING COAL in June. This time, the pair lean into warm, percussion-led Afropop, with lyrics centred on wealth,celebration and abundance. Ahead of its release on 12 November 2026, Wande Coal gave fans a taste of what was coming with a video staged as an owambe celebration inside a banking hall—a fitting preview for a song that takes its cues from the festive side of Nigerian life. ﻿ Patoranking featuring Olamide – “Welcome to Lagos” Keeping that celebratory mood going, Patoranking and Olamide join forces on “Welcome to Lagos” to give Nigeria’s commercial capital its own musical tribute. The Afro-dancehall collaboration captures the city’s familiar mix of hustle,nightlife and everyday movement, with both artists bringing their distinct sounds to the record. Patoranking opens with his dancehall delivery, setting the pace before Olamide takes over with Yoruba verses rooted in the city’s street culture.Released on 10 November 2026 alongside an official music video, the track gives two of Nigerian music’s established names a chance to celebrate the city that continues to inspire countless songs. ﻿ Khaid featuring King Dr. Saheed Osupa – “Yasin” Switching lanes from contemporary street anthems to a meeting of two musical eras, Khaid takes an unexpected turn on “Yasin” alongside Fuji veteran King Dr. Saheed Osupa . The song brings Khaid’s contemporary Afrobeats melodies together with Osupa’s traditional Fuji vocals and talking-drum rhythms, giving both artists room to draw on their distinct musical styles. An official lyric video followed on 14 November 2026. With this collaboration, Khaid steps beyond the sound audiences may be most familiar with, while Osupa brings his unmistakable Fuji influence to a new musical setting. ﻿ Spyro – “Kpan Kpan” If you are looking to pick up the tempo even further, Spyro keeps things firmly on the dancefloor with “Kpan Kpan”, a two-minute, 19-second Afropop release produced by Colonel Tyemmy . The track is built around bouncy percussion and a hook that is easy to pick up, making it a straightforward party selection. Released on 13 N

Produced by Grammy-winning producer Harmony “ HMoney ” Samuels , the song moves between Seyi Shay’s English verses and Vegedream’s French vocals, with both artists approaching the relationship from their own perspectives. item.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model
item.description: null As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines." The current version of Starship — the one that launched Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage. V3's Ship is 171 feet (52 m) tall and features six of SpaceX's Raptor V3 engines. (The similarly reusable Super Heavy V3 booster is powered by 33 Raptors.) So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk shared this chart depicting the evolution of SpaceX's Starship vehicles from the V2 to the planned V4 variant in August 2025. Exact specifications for Starship V4 are evolving. (Image credit: SpaceX/Elon Musk) Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon . Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g. View Deal To provide a little perspective about that vehicle's planned dimensions: The V4 Ship will be the same height as a fully stacked Falcon 9 , SpaceX's workhorse two-stage rocket, and much broader: Ship is 30 feet (9 m) across, while the Falcon 9's payload fairing is 17.1 feet (5.2 m) wide. This isn't the first we've heard about a V4 Starship. Back in August 2025, for example, Musk posted a graphic showing Starship's planned progression from the V2 to the V3 to the V4, which he said is expected to debut in 2027. That slide pegs the future Starship's total height at 466 feet (142 m), 200 feet (61 m) of which would be Ship. But those numbers are out of date, Musk stressed in the post, saying that V4 is "probably closer to 150m height." So, yeah: If all goes according to plan, the next Starship will be nearly 500 feet tall. item.content:encoded: null As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk shared this chart depicting the evolution of SpaceX's Starship vehicles from the V2 to the planned V4 variant in August 2025. Exact specifications for Starship V4 are evolving. (Image credit: SpaceX/Elon Musk) Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon . Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g. View Deal To provide a little perspective about that vehicle's planned dimensions: The V4 Ship will be the same height as a fully stacked Falcon 9 , SpaceX's workhorse two-stage rocket, and much broader: Ship is 30 feet (9 m) across, while the Falcon 9's payload fairing is 17.1 feet (5.2 m) wide. This isn't the first we've heard about a V4 Starship. Back in August 2025, for example, Musk posted a graphic showing Starship's planned progression from the V2 to the V3 to the V4, which he said is expected to debut in 2027. That slide pegs the future Starship's total height at 466 feet (142 m), 200 feet (61 m) of which would be Ship. But those numbers are out of date, Musk stressed in the post, saying that V4 is "probably closer to 150m height." So, yeah: If all goes according to plan, the next Starship will be nearly 500 feet tall. Starship V4 will be ~70m long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load.Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher thrust V4 engines. November 16, 2026 The original Starship Flight 15 mission plan called for a double chopsticks catch, with both Super Heavy and Ship coming back to the launch tower for recovery. This would have been feasible, as the catches were scheduled a day apart: Super Heavy would land just 6.5 minutes after launch, while Ship would circle Earth for 22.5 hours, and deploy a batch of SpaceX's Starlink V3 internet satellites, before coming home. (Ship ended up delivering the satellites as planned.) The twofer didn't happen, however; Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday as a result. But that wasn't a huge deal, as SpaceX had already pulled off Super Heavy catches on three previous Starship flights. The Ship catch was unprecedented, because it's been a taller order. Ship returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter. SpaceX hadn't even tried the maneuver before Flight 15, so executing it was a very big deal. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's Ship-landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes."

item.title: Tems Is Officially a 12-Time Grammy Nominee!
item.description: Tems is officially a 12-time Grammy nominee after securing four nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. Photo Credit: Tems/Instagram One, two, three… and now 12! Tems has added four more Grammy nominations to her record, bringing her career total to 12 ahead of the 69th Grammy Awards. The latest recognition also makes her the first Nigerian female artist to receive four nominations in a single Grammy year, with this year’s shortlist recognising her work across four categories. The Nigerian singer is in contention for Best Global Music Album with her 10-track EP, Love Is a Kingdom , and Best African Music Performance for “ Big Daddy ”. She has also earned nominations for Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “ What You Need ”. The four nominations give her one of the most extensive Nigerian representations at this year’s ceremony and bring her Grammy wins to two, following previous victories in 2023 and 2025. Her relationship with the Recording Academy began in 2022, when she received her first nomination for her contribution to Wizkid ‘s “ Essence ”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 64th Grammy Awards. The following year brought three more nominations, this time for her work on Future’s “ Wait for U ” featuring Drake and Beyoncé ‘s Renaissance . She won her first Grammy that night, taking home Best Melodic Rap Performance for “Wait for U”, while also receiving nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Song. Tems earned another nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards in 2024 for “ Lift Me Up ”, her contribution to the Black Panther : Wakanda Forever soundtrack, in the Best Song Written for Visual Media category. She returned to the Grammys the following year with three nominations, including Best Global Music Album for her debut album, Born in the Wild , and Best R&B Song for “ Burning ”. Her second Grammy win came in the Best African Music Performance category, where “ Love Me JeJe ” took home the award at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025. Now, with four nominations for the 69th edition, Tems has added another significant chapter to her Grammy record. The ceremony will take place on Sunday, 7 February 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. The post Tems Is Officially a 12-Time Grammy Nominee! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: What exactly is a light-day? Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe
item.description: null After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth. This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond. Astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA. Although the term light-day might sound like a measurement of time, it is actually a unit of distance, much like a light-year . Astronomers use light-based measurements because conventional miles and kilometers become increasingly difficult to comprehend when describing the enormous distances between objects in space. For perspective on how far Voyager 1 has travelled, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, meaning our planet is approximately 8.3 light-minutes from the sun. Radio signals traveling between Earth and Mars can take anywhere from three to 22 minutes, depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, according to the statement. By comparison, when Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth , a radio signal sent from the probe will take a full 24 hours to reach mission controllers on Earth, and a command transmitted from Earth will take another 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. A NASA visualization showing Voyager 1 looking back towards the solar system as it approaches one light-day away from Earth. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The communication delay affects how engineers operate spacecraft at such distances. Unlike spacecraft operating closer to Earth, which can receive commands and return data with relatively little delay, communicating with Voyager 1 requires mission controllers to account for the extended signal travel time when planning spacecraft operations, troubleshooting technical issues and evaluating the results of commands sent to the probe. Voyager 1 has been traveling away from Earth since its launch on Sept. 5, 1977 . Now cruising through interstellar space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 kph), the spacecraft has spent more than 49 years covering the distance that light can cross in a single day. Even at that speed, Voyager 1 is moving relatively slowly compared with light itself. Its twin, Voyager 2 , which launched in 1977 on a different trajectory, is expected to reach the same one-light-day milestone in November 2035. As Voyager 1 and, eventually, Voyager 2 continue their journeys through interstellar space , their growing distances from Earth offer a measure of both the reach of human exploration and the communication challenges

item.title: 'Maybe the scariest thing I've heard in my life': Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover reveals his toughest challenge before flying to the moon
item.description: null TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Former NASA astronaut Victor Glover has flown in combat, performed four spacewalks and strapped himself to the top of rockets launching into space. But before embarking on his historic Artemis II journey around the moon, he faced something even more difficult: a conversation with his four daughters. Speaking alongside former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, Glover opened up about the challenges of preparing his family for his riskiest mission yet. "This is maybe the greatest challenge of my astronaut career," Glover said. Glover joined NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1 , 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. But preparing for the historic journey wasn't just about mastering the spacecraft and executing the mission successfully. It also meant making sure his family was ready for what lay ahead. When Glover first traveled to space aboard SpaceX's Crew-1 mission in 2020, his children were much younger and he and his wife, Dionna, made a conscious effort to prepare them for his time in space. "We decided, as a parental unit, Dionna and I, that we were going to put as much effort into making sure our family was ready as NASA was putting into making sure I was ready to be a crew member," Glover explained. Victor Glover speaking at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, 2026. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic/Future) The family visited NASA's Kennedy Space Center , toured the launch pad and crew quarters and even planned when Glover would call home from the International Space Station . But by the time Artemis II came around, things were different. All four of his daughters were now adults, and preparing them for his journey around the moon meant discussing the mission's risks, including the possibility that he might not return home. Glover recalled his wife telling him something he described as maybe the scariest thing he'd ever heard. "You should have this talk with our daughters." And although he knew she was right, it wasn't an easy conversation to have. "We did, and it did not go well in my opinion," Glover admitted. "Well, it's not about going well. The talk needed to be done, just because it's hard." The following day, Glover sent his daughters and wife a poem, Live Your Life , by Chief Tecumseh. The poem helped Glover express something he had struggled to put into words during their conversation: why he believed the risks of traveling to the moon were worth taking. "It was a very tough conversation, but they understood that I know this is risky. I wasn't just telling them Dad's risking his life. Glover joined NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1 , 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. But preparing for the historic journey wasn't just about mastering the spacecraft and executing the mission successfully. It also meant making sure his family was ready for what lay ahead. When Glover first traveled to space aboard SpaceX's Crew-1 mission in 2020, his children were much younger and he and his wife, Dionna, made a conscious effort to prepare them for his time in space. "We decided, as a parental unit, Dionna and I, that we were going to put as much effort into making sure our family was ready as NASA was putting into making sure I was ready to be a crew member," Glover explained. Victor Glover speaking at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, 2026. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic/Future) The family visited NASA's Kennedy Space Center , toured the launch pad and crew quarters and even planned when Glover would call home from the International Space Station . But by the time Artemis II came around, things were different. All four of his daughters were now adults, and preparing them for his journey around the moon meant discussing the mission's risks, including the possibility that he might not return home. Glover recalled his wife telling him something he described as maybe the scariest thing he'd ever heard. "You should have this talk with our daughters." And although he knew she was right, it wasn't an easy conversation to have. "We did, and it did not go well in my opinion," Glover admitted. "Well, it's not about going well. The talk needed to be done, just because it's hard." The following day, Glover sent his daughters and wife a poem, Live Your Life , by Chief Tecumseh. The poem helped Glover express something he had struggled to put into words during their conversation: why he believed the risks of traveling to the moon were worth taking. "It was a very tough conversation, but they understood that I know this is risky. I wasn't just telling them Dad's risking his life. There's a real point to this and there's a reason to take this risk," Glover explained. "This poem helped me to say it in a way that I didn't have words for." After traveling around the moon and returning safely to Earth, one moment stood out above all others. When we asked Glover in a separate interview at Starmus on Oct. 20, which moment from Artemis II he would most like to relive, he answered immediately. "Splashdown." "It's the true, ultimate mission accomplishment. Just 'we did it.' We survived. My family is relieved, and there's just nothing like it," Glover explained. "There's nothing like coming home. There's nothing like returning to Earth." NASA astronaut Victor Glover, Artemis II pilot is assisted off the flight deck after a successful splashdown, arriving aboard USS John P. Murtha. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls)

item.title: Meet the Winners of the 2026 AWIEF Awards
item.description: The Africa Women Innovation and Entrepreneurship Forum ( AWIEF ) is pleased to announce the winners of its 2026 AWIEF Awards. Launched in 2017, the prestigious annual AWIEF Awards recognise, honour and celebrate outstanding women entrepreneurs, innovators, and leaders across various industry sectors for their achievements and contributions to Africa’s inclusive economic growth and development. The 2026 awards ceremony and gala dinner took place on 11 November 2026 at the Cape Town International Convention Centre (CTICC) as part of the AWIEF2026 Conference, which convened over 600 entrepreneurs, business leaders, investors, policymakers, development partners, and key stakeholders from across Africa and beyond. Following a highly competitive nominations process, this year’s winners represent an inspiring range of industries and African markets, reflecting the breadth of entrepreneurial talent, innovation, and impact across the continent. The 2026 awards recognised outstanding achievements across seven categories, including emerging entrepreneurial leaders, agricultural innovators, technology pioneers, creative visionaries, and individuals driving meaningful social impact. The Male Ally Award, introduced in 2026, recognises the important role of men in advancing women’s economic empowerment and championing greater inclusion and gender equality. The Lifetime Achievement Award honours an exceptional female leader whose decades of leadership, entrepreneurship, and public service have contributed significantly to Africa’s economic, social, and institutional development while paving the way for future generations of women leaders. 2026 AWIEF AWARDS WINNERS WOMAN TO WATCH AWARD Faith Nafula – Founder & CEO, Solar Spark Energy , Kenya AGRI AWARD Joyce Rugano – CEO, Ecorich Solutions , Kenya IMPACT FOR GOOD AWARD Echo Nomsa VanderWal – Executive Director, The Luke Commission, Eswatini CREATIVE VISIONARY AWARD Renuka Methil – Managing Editor, Forbes Africa, South Africa TECH PIONEER AWARD Quinter Ochieng – Founder & CEO, Chargebyte Africa , Kenya MALE ALLY AWARD John de Wit – Small Enterprise Foundation (SEF), South Africa LIFETIME ACHIEVEMENT AWARD Mary Okelo – P & M Investment, Kenya Celebrating Excellence and Inspiring the Next Generation The AWIEF Awards remain an important platform for recognising the individuals shaping Africa’s entrepreneurial and innovation landscape. Beyond celebrating individual achievements, the awards highlight the importance of entrepreneurship, inclusive leadership, innovation, and collaboration in driving sustainable economic growth across the continent. AWIEF congratulates all the 2026 winners and celebrates their outstanding contributions to Africa’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. item.title: ‘Spiraling’ Trailer: Toni Tones and Jim Iyke Star in Nigerian Psychological Thriller About an Affair Gone Wrong
item.description: The official trailer for Spiraling , a Nigerian psychological thriller starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys, The Smart Money Woman ), Jim Iyke (Bad Comments, Merry Men 2) , Seun Ajayi ((Japa, The Smart Money Woman ) and Folu Storms (Red Circle, Baby Farm) , has been unveiled ahead of the series’ release on November 26th. Set against the backdrop of a historic election, the series follows Sade (Tones), a successful tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair sets off a chain of deception and betrayal. Spiraling Series/Instagram What begins as a private indiscretion quickly threatens Sade’s relationships, reputation and everything she has worked to build. item.title: Davido, Tems & Ayra Starr Take 3 of 5 Best Global Music Album Spots at 2027 Grammys
item.description: Nigerian music stars Ayra Starr, Davido, and Tems claim three of the five slots in the Best Global Music Album category at the 69th Grammy Awards. The music industry in Nigeria is in a celebratory mood right now as three Nigerian artists — Davido , Tems , and Ayra Starr — are officially in the running for the prestigious Best Global Music Album award at the 69th Grammy Awards. Presented annually by the Recording Academy, the Best Global Music Album category honours full-length studio albums and extended plays that celebrate non-Western musical traditions and cross-cultural sounds from around the world. Claiming three out of the five available spots in a single year marks an extraordinary showing for Nigerian music on the international stage. Marking his sixth career Grammy nod, Davido is nominated for his sixth studio album, Oriadé . Released on 31 July 2026 to commemorate 15 years in the music industry, the 13-track project draws its title from the Yoruba words for destiny (“Ori”) and crown (“Adé”). Across songs featuring Black Sherif , Mayorkun , Fola , Leon Thomas , Aya Nakamura , and Llona , the album reflects on gratitude, ambition, and his musical roots across Afrobeats, R&B, and amapiano. This nod follows three nominations at the 66th Grammys in 2024 ( Timeless for Best Global Music Album, “ Feel ” for Best Global Music Performance, and “ Unavailable ” featuring Musa Keys for Best African Music Performance), a nomination in 2025 for “ Sensational ” alongside Chris Brown and Lojay , and a 2026 nod for “ With You ” featuring Omah Lay . Tems is also competing for the prize with her seven-track extended play, Love Is a Kingdom , which arrived as a surprise release on 21 November 2025. Built around alternative R&B and Afrobeats rhythms, the project explores romance, self-worth, and spiritual reflection across tracks including “ First “, “ Big Daddy “, “ Lagos Love “, and “ What You Need “. Beyond her album recognition, Tems leads the Nigerian contingent at the 69th Grammy Awards with four nominations in total, becoming the first Nigerian female artist to earn four nods in a single year. She is also nominated for Best African Music Performance for “Big Daddy”, as well as Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “What You Need”. A two-time Grammy winner, she previously claimed Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s “Wait for U” featuring Drake, and Best African Music Performance in 2025 for “ Love Me JeJe “, while her debut album Born in the Wild was nominated in this global album category in 2025. Rounding out the Nigerian trio is Ayra Starr , who makes her debut appearance in the Best Global Music Album category with her third studio album, Starrgirl . Released on 14 August 2026, the 15-track album captures her growth and confidence across songs such as “ Tornado “, “ Heaven Baby ” featuring Zayn , “ Hot Body “, “ Who’s Dat Girl ” with Rema , and “ Gimme Dat ” with Wizkid . item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Have a question for Jonathan? Email soccerwithjw@theguardian.com , and he’ll answer the best in a future edition. Continue reading...

item.title: MSS Celebrates 20 Years of Industry Leadership, Unveils New Brand Identity and Future Growth Vision
item.description: Nigeria’s leading event technology company, Mobile Screens and Sound Limited ( MSS ), has marked two decades of pioneering innovation, industry transformation and excellence with a landmark gala held on Thursday, October 8, at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos. The event, themed The Art of Experience, brought together an influential gathering of business leaders, government officials, industry stakeholders, clients, partners and friends of the brand to celebrate a company whose innovations have helped shape the modern events landscape in Nigeria. For 20 years, MSS has remained at the forefront of event technology, delivering the sound, visuals, staging and technical expertise behind some of Nigeria’s most significant corporate, entertainment, government and cultural events. From introducing cutting-edge LED screen technology at a time when it was largely unfamiliar to the market, to becoming one of the country’s most trusted providers of integrated event production solutions, MSS has consistently redefined what is possible in the live experiences industry. The evening showcased the company’s remarkable journey from a bold entrepreneurial venture into an industry leader whose footprint extends across every facet of event technology. Through immersive storytelling, visual displays and experiential installations, guests were taken through the evolution of MSS and the pivotal role it has played in raising industry standards and inspiring the growth of an entire ecosystem of event technology providers. Reflecting on the company’s journey, Founder and Managing Director, Tunbosun Kola-Daisi , said: “Twenty years ago, we entered an industry where the solutions we offered were largely unfamiliar and where belief in the future of event technology was limited. LED screens, which are commonplace today, were then considered a novelty. The early years tested our resilience, and it took nearly five years before we broke even. But we remained steadfast in our vision because we understood the transformative power of technology in creating unforgettable experiences. Today, as we celebrate this milestone, we are proud not only of what we have built, but of the role MSS has played in shaping an industry, creating opportunities and setting new standards for excellence.” A defining moment of the evening was the unveiling of the company’s new logo and refreshed brand identity, signalling a bold new chapter in MSS’ evolution. The rebrand reflects the company’s growth and reinforces its position as a comprehensive provider of event technology solutions spanning sound, lighting, screens, production services, and immersive audience experiences. The unveiling culminated in a spectacular drone display that illuminated the Lagos skyline, symbolising the innovation, ambition and creativity that have defined the MSS journey for two decades. The event, themed The Art of Experience, brought together an influential gathering of business leaders, government officials, industry stakeholders, clients, partners and friends of the brand to celebrate a company whose innovations have helped shape the modern events landscape in Nigeria. For 20 years, MSS has remained at the forefront of event technology, delivering the sound, visuals, staging and technical expertise behind some of Nigeria’s most significant corporate, entertainment, government and cultural events. From introducing cutting-edge LED screen technology at a time when it was largely unfamiliar to the market, to becoming one of the country’s most trusted providers of integrated event production solutions, MSS has consistently redefined what is possible in the live experiences industry. The evening showcased the company’s remarkable journey from a bold entrepreneurial venture into an industry leader whose footprint extends across every facet of event technology. Through immersive storytelling, visual displays and experiential installations, guests were taken through the evolution of MSS and the pivotal role it has played in raising industry standards and inspiring the growth of an entire ecosystem of event technology providers. Reflecting on the company’s journey, Founder and Managing Director, Tunbosun Kola-Daisi , said: “Twenty years ago, we entered an industry where the solutions we offered were largely unfamiliar and where belief in the future of event technology was limited. LED screens, which are commonplace today, were then considered a novelty. The early years tested our resilience, and it took nearly five years before we broke even. But we remained steadfast in our vision because we understood the transformative power of technology in creating unforgettable experiences. Today, as we celebrate this milestone, we are proud not only of what we have built, but of the role MSS has played in shaping an industry, creating opportunities and setting new standards for excellence.” A defining moment of the evening was the unveiling of the company’s new logo and refreshed brand identity, signalling a bold new chapter in MSS’ evolution. The rebrand reflects the company’s growth and reinforces its position as a comprehensive provider of event technology solutions spanning sound, lighting, screens, production services, and immersive audience experiences. The unveiling culminated in a spectacular drone display that illuminated the Lagos skyline, symbolising the innovation, ambition and creativity that have defined the MSS journey for two decades. Speaking on the company’s future direction, Kola-Daisi added: “What began as a vision to transform event experiences has evolved into a business capable of powering some of the largest and most complex productions in Nigeria. Today, we can deliver large-scale sound reinforcement across major venues, deploy screens simultaneously across multiple events, support uninterrupted operations through an extensive power infrastructure, execute nationwide advertising installations, transform physical spaces into immersive experience centres, and provide end-to-end production management for events of every scale. But this is only the beginning. Our next chapter is focused on deeper innovation, strategic expansion across Africa and investing in the people who will drive the future of this industry. We are committed to remaining the benchmark for event technology excellence while building the next generation of industry professionals.” The anniversary celebration also highlighted MSS’ commitment to developing talent through the recently launched MSS Event Tech Academy, a pioneering capacity-building initiative designed to address the growing demand for skilled professionals within the event technology ecosystem. Delivered in partnership with KolaDaisi University, the intensive 10- week programme provided participants with both technical and practical training across six specialist areas: LED Screen Engineering, Sound Engineering, Camera Craft and Video Production, Lighting Design and Control, Event Management and Production, and Rigging and Trussing. More than 60 students completed the inaugural programme, gaining valuable hands-on experience through participation in live MSS projects and productions. Demonstrating the academy’s tangible impact, five graduates secured immediate employment with MSS upon completion of the programme. As Nigeria’s event technology industry continues to evolve, MSS remains committed to advancing professional standards, nurturing talent and driving innovation that elevates live experiences across the continent. Twenty years after helping pioneer a new era of event technology in Nigeria, MSS continues to set the pace, proving that exceptional experiences are not merely produced, but carefully engineered. About Mobile Screens and Sound Limited (MSS) Mobile Screens and Sound Limited (MSS) is Nigeria’s leading event technology company, delivering world-class solutions across sound, lighting, LED displays, staging, live production and experiential event management. With two decades of industry leadership, MSS has powered some of the country’s most notable live, corporate and entertainment events while championing innovation, professional excellence and talent development within the event technology sector. item.title: The Glenlivet Introduces a Three-Day Immersive Experience in Lagos
item.description: Lagos has no shortage of events, but from 19 to 21 November, The Glenlivet is planning something a little different. For three nights, Lagos will host The Glenlivet Experience, a curated immersion into the heritage, craftsmanship and distinctive character of the iconic Speyside single malt Scotch whisky, brought to life through a distinctly Lagos lens. Across the three days, The Glenlivet’s Brand Ambassadors, Ebuka Obi-Uchendu , Osas Ighodaro and Farooq Oreagba, will join the brand’s Tastemakers and guests from across culture, business, fashion, music and hospitality. Evane Chenuet, Marketing Director, Pernod Ricard Nigeria, said: “We wanted people to experience The Glenlivet single malt whisky rather than simply hear about it. The Glenlivet Experience brings our rich brand’s heritage to life in a way that feels contemporary, culturally relevant and that immerses our guests in our spirit of originality .” The first two days will welcome a curated audience, while on 21st November, the Experience will extend its invitation to a wider community, offering more guests the opportunity to discover the world of The Glenlivet. item.title: Asake, Tems, Wizkid & Ayra Starr Lead African Acts Nominated for 2027 Grammys
item.description: Tems, Asake, and Ayra Starr lead the stellar lineup of African nominees contending for Best African Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards. The Recording Academy has just rolled out the official nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards, and the Best African Music Performance category is an absolute powerhouse lineup with Nigerian artists making up a significant part of this year’s shortlist. Leading the category is Asake , who pulled off an incredible double entry in the category. He picked up a solo nod for his standout track “ Gratitude ” alongside a stellar collaborative nomination for “ Jogodo ” alongside Wizkid . For Wizkid, this latest nomination adds another major chapter to his historic Grammy legacy, building on his previous career milestones, which include his historic win for Best Music Video with Beyoncé for “ Brown Skin Girl ” at the 63rd Grammy Awards in 2021, as well as multiple past nominations. Tems is another Nigerian nominee, returning to the category she won at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025 with “ Love Me JeJe ”. This time, she is nominated for “ Big Daddy ”. Her previous Grammy win came in 2023, when she received Best Melodic Rap Performance for her contribution to Future ‘s “ Wait for U ”, featuring Drake . The Nigerian representation also includes Ayra Starr , whose nomination comes through “ Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?) ”, a collaboration with Beninese music legend Angélique Kidjo . Ayra Starr previously received a nomination in the category for “ Rush ”, while Angélique Kidjo brings her own Grammy-winning history to the collaboration, with wins for albums including Eve , Sings , Celia and Mother Nature . Rounding out the category with rich cultural resonance are Ghanaian musicians King Ayisoba and Rocky Dawuni , who earned a brilliant nomination for “ No Tradition, No Africa “. The 69th Grammy Awards will hold on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. item.title: Nora Awolowo, Teniola Aladese & Hero Daniels Win Big at The Future Awards Africa 2026 | See Full List
item.description: Nigerian actress, trained lawyer, and TFAA co-host Genoveva Umeh dressed for the 20th edition of The Future Awards Africa. Photo Credit: The Future Awards Africa/Instagram A historic hosting line-up spanning five African countries and the introduction of a first-of-its-kind AI assistant named Infinity marked the 20th edition of The Future Awards Africa (TFAA), held on Saturday, 14 November 2026, at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos. Themed “Celebrating The Redefiners: Africa’s AI Generation,” the ceremony recognised young Africans aged 18 to 35 across 26 categories, including technology and innovation, entrepreneurship, governance, music, film, literature, advocacy, sports and fashion. The anniversary edition was hosted by five personalities from across the continent: Nigerian actress and trained lawyer Genoveva Umeh ; Kenyan media personality Claudia Naisabwa ; Malawian radio broadcaster and television personality Priscilla Kayira ; Botswana television and radio host Resego Motlhokathari ; and Tanzanian actor and former Big Brother Africa winner Idris Sultan . Co-hosts Genoveva Umeh, Resego Motlhokathari, Claudia Naisabwa, Idris Sultan, and Priscilla Kayira pose together ahead of the 20th anniversary ceremony. Photo Credit: The Future Awards Africa/Instagram They shared the stage with Infinity, an AI assistant that interacted with the hosts through quick-witted and playful responses, drawing laughter from guests throughout the ceremony. Its introduction brought artificial intelligence into the evening’s entertainment, while musical performances by Sharp Band and the Loud Urban Choir added to the celebrations. Among the evening’s major winners, Nora Awolowo received the Prize for Young Person of the Year, Teniola Aladese won the Prize for Acting, and Olamidun Ogundoyin took home the Prize for Entrepreneurship. Pastor Jerry Uchechukwu Eze , represented at the ceremony by media personality Hero Daniels , received the Prize for Service to Young People. The ceremony also welcomed representatives of distinguished public figures, including Mobolaji Abubakre Ogunlende , Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, who represented Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu . Another highlight was the recognition of the first winners of The Future Awards Africa Independent (TFAAi), a state-level initiative established in 2026 to spotlight young changemakers whose contributions may receive limited attention on national platforms. Its first edition covered Rivers, Abia, Oyo and Kano States, extending the awards’ reach into more communities. Daniel Ekpe (Awkaman) accepts his award on stage at the 20th anniversary edition of The Future Awards Africa. Photo Credit: Daniel Ekpe/Instagram Reflecting on the milestone, Ayodeji Razaq , Executive Director of The Future Awards Africa, said the 20th edition represented a sustained commitment to recognising young Africans shaping the continent’s future. Photo Credit: The Future Awards Africa/Instagram They shared the stage with Infinity, an AI assistant that interacted with the hosts through quick-witted and playful responses, drawing laughter from guests throughout the ceremony. Its introduction brought artificial intelligence into the evening’s entertainment, while musical performances by Sharp Band and the Loud Urban Choir added to the celebrations. Among the evening’s major winners, Nora Awolowo received the Prize for Young Person of the Year, Teniola Aladese won the Prize for Acting, and Olamidun Ogundoyin took home the Prize for Entrepreneurship. Pastor Jerry Uchechukwu Eze , represented at the ceremony by media personality Hero Daniels , received the Prize for Service to Young People. The ceremony also welcomed representatives of distinguished public figures, including Mobolaji Abubakre Ogunlende , Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, who represented Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu . Another highlight was the recognition of the first winners of The Future Awards Africa Independent (TFAAi), a state-level initiative established in 2026 to spotlight young changemakers whose contributions may receive limited attention on national platforms. Its first edition covered Rivers, Abia, Oyo and Kano States, extending the awards’ reach into more communities. Daniel Ekpe (Awkaman) accepts his award on stage at the 20th anniversary edition of The Future Awards Africa. Photo Credit: Daniel Ekpe/Instagram Reflecting on the milestone, Ayodeji Razaq , Executive Director of The Future Awards Africa, said the 20th edition represented a sustained commitment to recognising young Africans shaping the continent’s future. He also highlighted TFAAi as part of the platform’s effort to ensure exceptional work receives recognition wherever it happens. TFAA co-founders Chude Jideonwo and Adebola Williams also reflected on the platform’s journey and the generations of young achievers whose stories have shaped its history. Twenty editions on, The Future Awards Africa continues to recognise young Africans making significant contributions across different fields, while creating room for new voices and achievements across the continent. Below is the full list of winners from the 20th edition of The Future Awards Africa: Young Person of the Year Nora Awolowo Acting Teniola Aladese Technology & Innovation Maxwell Opondo Law Dr Stanley U Nweke-Eze Film Jigar Ganatra Health and Wellness Mobolaji Ajayi Fashion Desiree Iyama Activism and Advocacy Habib Sheidu Music Samuel Damilare (Abefe) Lifestyle Content Creation Omotolani Tayo-Osikoya (Chef T) Comedy Content Creation Daniel Ekpe (Awkaman) Professional Service Fatou Jeng Creative Excellence Emmanuel Whajah Community Action Oluwadamilola Atinuke Feyide Entrepreneurship Olamidun Ogundoyin Arts Blessing Ejiroghene Adewale Literature Fatimah Bala Governance Emma Inamutila Theofelus Journalism Riyah Abdul Education Chinwendu Monalisa Agbata Service to Young People Pastor Jerry Uchechukwu Eze Sport Nene Joy Ojo On Air Personality Joey Akan Performing Arts Ibukunoluwa Oluyinka Ajagbe Agriculture Adaeze Akpagbula Photography Oluwatosin Junaid Energy and Sustainability Damilola Hamid Balogun The post Nora Awolowo, Teniola Aladese & Hero Daniels Win Big at The Future Awards Africa 2026 | See Full List appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. Continue reading...

item.title: A long wait, some magic and that smile: Ronaldinho savours Ravenna debut at 46

In June, the former Barcelona and Brazil legend Ronaldinho was unveiled by the Serie C side Ravenna to make his comeback at the age of 46 – 11 years after his last official game. Then silence. But on a chilly November day on the eastern coast of Italy, there he was , not only in the squad, but in the starting XI for the eagerly anticipated derby against Forlì as Ravenna chase promotion. item.title: Tiyani Makamu Wins Miss South Africa 2026!
item.description: Tiyani Makamu celebrates on stage moments after being crowned Miss South Africa 2026 at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg on 14 November 2026. Photo Credit: Miss South Africa/Instagram South Africa has a new queen, and her name is Tiyani Makamu ! At a stylish finale held at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the 27-year-old entrepreneur and youth advocate from Bronkhorstspruit, Gauteng stepped forward to claim the Miss South Africa 2026 crown. Outgoing titleholder Qhawekazi Mazaleni handed over the reins, while Cwenga Koyana Kotu-Rammopo from Edenvale and Lesego Khumo Nyathela from Springs took home the First Princess and Second Princess titles. Away from the pageant stage, Tiyani Makamu already wears plenty of impressive hats. A graduate of the Pearson Institute of Higher Education, she works as a communications professional, Group Digital Lead, and Client Success Executive, and also runs Hubsela—a small-business support platform she founded to help fellow entrepreneurs build thriving ventures. Her passion for youth employment and business education also shows up in her community work, including supporting a local library initiative in Ivory Park to help young people gain practical skills. Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu, entrepreneur and founder of Hubsela from Bronkhorstspruit, Gauteng. Photo Credit: Miss South Africa/Instagram What makes Tiyani Makamu’s reign especially exciting is how different Miss South Africa 2026 looks this year. Under the Motsepe Group of Companies’ ownership, the Miss South Africa Organisation shifted its focus toward homegrown leadership and social impact—meaning neither Makamu nor her runners-up will head off to international competitions like Miss Universe, Miss World, or Miss Supranational. Instead, she gets to pour her entire year into community projects across South Africa through the pageant’s Empower Youth Africa initiative, backed by a R1 million cash prize and access to up to R500,000 from the Impact Fund. Chatting shortly after her crowning at the Sandton Convention Centre—which hosted the finale for the first time after four years in Pretoria—Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu shared what she hopes to accomplish over the next twelve months: My mandate as Miss South Africa is to empower women entrepreneurs by bridging the gaps in access to opportunities, business development and funding. I want to equip women with the skills, resources and financial readiness to build sustainable, thriving businesses. Through entrepreneurship and skills development, I aim to champion the economic empowerme nt of women and youth across Afr ica. Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu, who will dedicate her reign to domestic entrepreneurship and youth empowerment across South Africa. Photo Credit: Tiyani Makamu/Instagram The post Tiyani Makamu Wins Miss South Africa 2026! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne Wrack Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City Continue reading...

item.title: Republic of Ireland have plenty of promise, but are unable to shake self-sabotage
item.description: Hopes of promotion remain alive, but another costly collapse has raised familiar questions before the decisive Nations League game with Kosovo The Republic of Ireland stand on the verge, although of what, nobody seems quite sure. Tuesday’s final Nations League group match, at home to Kosovo, presents a chance for progress or yet another opportunity to showcase a frustrating habit of messing things up. For 78 minutes in Linz on Saturday, Heimir Hallgrímsson’s side gave as good as they got against an Austria side who had not lost at home for a little more than three years. Set up in a compact, attack-minded formation they carried credible threat against hosts managed by Ralf Rangnick, but to nobody’s great surprise Sasa Kalajdzic broke the deadlock, scrambling home the winner from a needlessly conceded and poorly defended corner. Continue reading...

item.title: Celebrating African Music, Culture and Connection! Here’s a Rundown of My SIMA 2026 Experience
item.description: In the words of a sage, the reason we go and come back is so that we have tales to tell. Last week, I told you I was headed to Cotonou and invited you to come along. If you followed on Instagram, well done! Now, I must tell you even more tales of this journey! Welcome, my dear BNers, to my entire rundown of the amazing SIMA 2026, which was held in Cotonou, Benin Republic. From November 12–13, 2026, Cotonou, Republic of Benin, hosted the third edition of the Salon des Industries Musicales d’Afrique Francophone (SIMA), bringing together artists, music executives, creatives, policymakers and industry professionals from across Africa and beyond. This year’s theme, African Music: From the Stage to Global Influence , explored an important question: How do we translate the global influence of African music into sustainable economic opportunities for the people and industries behind it? As someone who loves music and storytelling, I was particularly excited to experience these conversations firsthand and share them with you. So let’s get into it. First things first, Bonjour Cotonou! View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Now, let’s get into Day 1 of SIMA. I decided to channel my inner choir girl with my black-and-white ensemble and my DIY necktie, giving a nod to the essence of the event — music. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) If you still don’t get the full picture, I break down what SIMA really is all about here. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) I went on to experience very enlightening conversations amongst industry professionals and experts. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) One of my conversations was with Mamby Diomandé , Founder and Co-Founder of SIMA, who shared insights into the vision behind the platform and its continued expansion. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) I also caught up with the Executive Director of Livespot, Solomon Sonaiya. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Now, this was one part of SIMA 2026 that particularly caught my attention. A panel presented a baseline study of women in the Nigerian music industry. And even more exciting was the official launch of VERA, a network dedicated to women in the music industry, alongside its VERA Mentorship Programme. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Now, let’s get into Day 2! From the music to even more insightful conversations, it’s safe to say I had a ball!
